turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]

turns.text: Maybe in October. We're stretched thin with open enrollment prep.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]

turns.text: Thanks. And hey, tell your garden I said good luck.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hi [PERSON_1], hi [PERSON_2]. [PERSON_3] here. Thanks for making the time today.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_3]. Good to be on. I'm out in the truck between jobs, so if I drop for a second it's just the parking lot.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hi [PERSON_3]. I've got the calendar open, so I can grab dates while we talk.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. The plan for today is mostly logistics. Where we are with the account setup, training dates, who needs access, and what the next couple of weeks look like. Sound okay?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Works for us.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Great. So the tracking numbers are live across the six locations. [PERSON_2], you saw the test calls come through on Friday?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I did. I made three calls from my cell and one from the office line and they all showed up with the right location attached.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. And the tag is on the website, so dynamic number insertion is swapping the numbers per campaign. That part looked clean on my end.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yep, I spot checked a couple of landing pages and the numbers were changing like they should.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: What about the Google Ads side? Are the conversions flowing yet?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's connected. The offline conversions are set to send once a call qualifies, and it matches on the click ID. It can take a day or two before you see it reflected in the ads reporting.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay. We don't need to watch it that closely, but good to know it's on.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Now, training. I usually do two sessions, one for the folks answering phones and one for you two on the reporting side. Does that split make sense?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yes, please. The front desk people need the call handling part more than the dashboards.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: How many people would be in the first session?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Probably five. Two at the Raleigh office, one in Durham, one in Greensboro, one in Charlotte. The other locations are smaller and the managers there mostly answer their own phones.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. And for the second session, just you and [PERSON_1]?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Probably me, [PERSON_2], and our office manager Renata. She handles a lot of the scheduling and she'll be in the tool more than I am.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Renata, okay. I'll add her to the invite. What's her email?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll send it to you after the call, I don't have it memorized.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: No rush. Let's talk dates. I have Tuesday the 22nd and Thursday the 24th open in the morning. Would a 9:30 start work for the front desk group?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Tuesdays are usually lighter for us, so the 22nd at 9:30 is better.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Let's book that. An hour should cover it. And then the reporting session, does the 24th at 9:30 work, or would you rather do the following week?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: The 24th is fine. Mornings before ten are good for me, I'm usually still in the office doing paperwork.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Great. I'll send both invites today with a join link and a short agenda. [PERSON_2], do you want me to send the agenda to you first so you can add anything?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Sure, send it over and I'll forward it to the group.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Will do. How's the call volume looking right now? I know fall is a busy stretch for pest work.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's picking up. We're probably at 400 to 450 calls a month across the locations, and it'll climb once the weather turns. Termite inspections drive a lot of it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And the lawn side slows down in November, so the mix shifts. More pest, less lawn.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That lines up with what I usually see. Anything changing on your side before the training? New numbers, new campaigns?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Not right now. We might add a campaign for the Charlotte area in October, but that's not confirmed yet.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. If it happens, just let me know and we can make sure the number is set up before it goes live.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sounds good.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: One more thing on logistics. Who should have admin access besides the two of you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Just us for now. I'd rather keep it tight while we're getting used to it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's fine. You can add people later whenever you want. And the billing contact is still you, [PERSON_1]?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yes, that's me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. So to recap the action items, I'll send the two training invites for the 22nd and 24th at 9:30, plus an agenda for [PERSON_2] to review. [PERSON_2] will send me Renata's email so I can add her. Anything else you want on the list?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I don't think so. That covers it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Nothing from me. Thanks [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks both. Talk to you on the 22nd.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Sounds good, bye.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Bye.

turns.text: We're a bit above that now. August came in around fifty-one thousand, and September is tracking similar.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's a decent jump.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, the fiber bundle campaign is doing well. Google Ads is spending more, so more calls are coming in.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And the offline conversions are still landing in Google Ads okay?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Far as I know, yeah. Nothing's come up on that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good. [PERSON_3], I wanted to check in on the PreSense side. You flagged something a couple weeks back about screen pops.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I did, and it's still happening. Here's the thing. When Genesys transfers a call from one queue to another, or from one agent to another, the receiving agent gets a blank screen pop.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Nothing in it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So the pop fires, it just has no data in it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Right. The agent sees the PreSense window come up but there's no journey, no pages, no ad. So they end up asking the caller what they were looking at, which is exactly what we bought this to avoid.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: How often is it happening?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: It's not every transfer, but it's often enough that my supervisors are noticing. Probably a handful a day per queue, more on the busier ones.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It's coming up in our sales huddles too. The agents on the receiving end are the ones complaining.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay. Is it specific to certain queues, or is it any transfer?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Any transfer as far as I can tell. We tried it on the wireless queue and the fiber queue, same result.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And is this happening on warm transfers, cold transfers, or both?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Both. We tested it with a couple of supervisors watching.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Got it. I want to get this in front of the right folks with the details you just gave me. Can you send me a couple of call IDs where it happened?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That'll help them trace it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah, I can pull those this afternoon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Perfect. I'll take it back to the team and see what we can find out. I won't promise anything on timing yet, but I'll keep you posted.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That works. Thanks, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Anything else on the list today?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I think we're good. Oh, one thing. Can we move our next check-in to the Tuesday instead of Wednesday? I've got a conflict that week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sure, I'll send a new invite. Anything else, or should I let you both get back to it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's it from me. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sounds good. Thanks, both. Talk soon.

turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:56 The second one, mostly. If it were one bundled price at roughly what we pay now, she'd sign tomorrow. But she's not going to defend four separate increases line by line.

turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:09 That's helpful. Let me get this in front of our deal desk and see what a single bundled structure could look like. I can't promise the number yet, but the packaging question is fair.

[PERSON_1] and [PERSON_2] confirmed the core pieces are in place and asked for the next [PERSON_6] date. No open items on the Invoca side.

turns.text: the next QM refresher for the scheduling supervisors is penciled in for October 6 at 10:00 AM CT. [PERSON_1] will confirm room availability by September 25.

turns.text: confirm October 6 [PERSON_6] room and send calendar invite by September 25.

turns.text: schedule a 15-minute pre-[PERSON_6] check-in with [PERSON_2] for October 2.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Morning [PERSON_1], morning [PERSON_2]. How are things in Austin?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Morning [PERSON_3]. Things are good, busy. We're heading into what is usually our busiest stretch for residential solar in Texas, so we're getting the team ready.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, and the Spanish side is already seeing more calls, especially from the Meta campaigns. It's good, but we want to make sure we're staffed right.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That makes sense. September and October have been heavy for you the last couple of years. Do you have a sense of how much call volume you're expecting?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We're planning for about a 30 percent increase over the summer baseline. Last year we hit around 4,200 calls a month in that window, and this year we're hoping to be closer to 5,500.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, so a meaningful jump. Are you adding seats on the Invoca side for that?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We are. We're bringing on eight new sales reps, mostly on the Spanish team, and two more on the English side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So that's ten new users to provision.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And a couple of them are starting next Monday, so we'd like them to have access before then if possible.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Let me pull up your user list. I can get the provisioning request started today. Do you have the names and emails ready?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: [PERSON_2] has the list. He can send it over after this call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yes, I'll send it this afternoon. I have all ten with their emails. I'll also note which team they're on so the permissions are right.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. Once I have that, I'll submit the request and we should have them set up within two business days. That gets you ahead of Monday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good. And speaking of training, we'd like to do a refresher for the whole team before the rush really hits. Is there a date that works on your side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Let me check the calendar. I have the week of September 28 open. Would a Tuesday or Wednesday work?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Wednesday the 30th would be better. Tuesdays we have our pipeline review in the morning.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, Wednesday the 30th. What time?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Could we do 10 AM Central? That gives the West Coast folks time to get in.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: 10 AM Central works. I'll send an invite and we can do a 45 minute session, with maybe 15 minutes for questions at the end.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That sounds good. Can we make sure the Spanish team gets a separate session too? Sometimes the examples in English don't land the same way.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Of course. We can do a second session in Spanish, maybe the following day, Thursday the 1st. Same time?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thursday the 1st at 10, that works. I'll let the team know.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And [PERSON_3], one more logistics thing. We're going to be running some new Google Ads campaigns in Arizona and Florida starting mid-October.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We want to make sure the tracking numbers are set up correctly.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. Do you have the campaign details yet, or is that still in progress?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Still in progress. Our media team is finalizing the creative, but we expect to have the campaigns live by October 15.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We'll need new tracking numbers for each campaign and state.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, so roughly two weeks out. I can help coordinate with our provisioning team once you have the final list. Just send me the campaign names and the states, and we'll get the numbers set up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Will those numbers also flow into Salesforce the same way? We rely on that for follow-up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: They should, as long as the campaigns are mapped correctly. We'll confirm that when we set them up. I'll make a note to check the Salesforce integration settings with you.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Great. And one last thing, we're planning a team offsite in early November, just a half day. Would you be able to join us for a quick update on any new features or best practices?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'd be happy to. What date are you thinking?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We're looking at November 5th, in the morning. It would be in Austin, so you'd have to come to us.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's fine. I'll check my travel schedule and confirm. I can put together a short session, maybe 30 minutes, on anything you want to cover.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That would be helpful. The team always likes seeing you.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Same here. Alright, so to recap, [PERSON_2] sends the user list today, I'll get those ten seats provisioned. We have training on the 30th in English and the 1st in Spanish.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll follow up on the Arizona and Florida tracking numbers once you have the campaign details. And I'll check on the November 5th offsite.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That covers everything. Thanks [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thanks [PERSON_3], talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks both. Have a good one.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hi [PERSON_1], thanks for grabbing the time. How's your week going over there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_2]. Busy, but that's normal for September. We're heading into storm season, so claims volume is starting to climb.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Makes sense. I saw the call volume ticked up about twelve percent month over month across your tracking numbers. Is that the storm activity or just seasonal?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Mostly seasonal, plus the new home bundle campaign that marketing launched on the fifteenth. That one's been driving a lot of after-hours calls.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay so that brings me to something I wanted to check in on. How's the AI Voice Agent pilot going on the after-hours claims intake?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Mostly good. It's catching calls that would have gone to voicemail, and the transcripts are way better than I expected. But there's one thing that's been bugging my team.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Tell me more.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: When the AI agent transfers over to one of our live reps, the information it gathered doesn't show up on the Genesys screen.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So the rep is starting from scratch, and the caller has to repeat their account number or policy number all over again.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It makes us look disorganized.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. Does that happen on every transfer, or only some of them?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Every transfer I've listened to so far, which is maybe a dozen calls. My supervisor pulled a few recordings this week and saw the same thing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And when you say the information doesn't show up, is that the AI's summary, or the raw details like name and claim number?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Both, really. The rep sees the incoming call but nothing the agent collected. No name, no policy, no reason for the call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, let me take that back to the team and see what we're working with. Can you send me two or three call IDs from this week?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That'll help.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sure, I'll pull them this afternoon. I've got a list in the pilot tracker.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Perfect. Anything else on the pilot side? How's the after-hours coverage looking?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Coverage is fine. We've got two new hires starting on the twenty-eighth, so that'll help with the queue once they're trained.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Nice. Are they going through the standard onboarding, or something different for the after-hours team?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Standard. My team lead is handling it. They'll shadow for a week and then take live calls.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. Let me know if you want a refresher on the QM scorecards for that group. I know the new hires will be scored on the claims intake card.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's probably fine. The scorecards have been working well. No complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good to hear. And what about the Google Ads side? Any shifts in spend you want me to know about?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not really. Marketing handles that. They mentioned they're happy with the offline conversion match rates.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. I'll leave that with them. Now, on the transfer thing, just so I have it straight. Is it happening on every after-hours call that hits the AI agent and then goes to a live rep?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Every one we've checked. It doesn't seem to matter which queue or which rep. The details just don't land.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Understood. I'll open a case and keep you posted. In the meantime, are your reps working around it somehow?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: They're just asking the caller to repeat themselves. It's not the end of the world, but it's not great for the member experience either.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, I get that. I'll flag it with the product team and see what we can find. Probably need the call IDs before I can say much more.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Fair enough. I'll send those over today.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thanks. Before I let you go, is there anything else on your list? Anything coming up that I should know about?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not really. We're in good shape otherwise. The only thing is my director wants a quick readout on the pilot by mid-October, so if you have any early data, that'd help.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I can put together a short summary from the dashboards. What kind of numbers does she want to see?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Containment rate, average handle time, and how many calls the AI is catching after hours. Just a page or so.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. I'll have something for you the week of the fifth. That gives us a little buffer before your deadline.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That works.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, so to recap, I'll open the case on the transfer details, you'll send call IDs today, and I'll send a pilot summary in early October.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sounds right. Thanks [PERSON_2].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Any time. I'll follow up by Monday either way. Have a good one, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: You too. Talk soon.

turns.text: Hey [PERSON_3]. Good, busy. It's been hot, so HVAC is still humming along.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, we're in the middle of a heat wave, so the phones are nonstop.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I bet. I saw the volume tick up in I mean, the dashboard, looks like you're tracking toward, what, 12,000 calls this month?

turns.text: Yeah, we're at about 11,800 so far, so probably closer to 13,000 by the 30th.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: You know, Nice. And how's the PreSense rollout going? I know you added it mid-term.

turns.text: It's fine. The screen pops are showing up for the agents. No issues there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, that's been good. But I wanted to talk about the Google Ads piece. That's why I asked for this call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, let's dig in. What's going on?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So we send offline call conversions to Google Ads. I mean, and I've been noticing they land one to three days after the call. Sometimes longer.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. And that's a change from what you were seeing before?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It's been like this for a few weeks. Uh, it used to be same day, mostly. Now I'm pulling reports and half the conversions from Monday aren't in Google until Wednesday or Thursday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And that's a problem because we're bidding on Smart Bidding. If Google's optimizing on incomplete data, it's it's making decisions on a partial picture.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Right. So the conversions are eventually getting there, but the delay means the bidding algorithm is working with stale info.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Exactly. And last week we had a campaign where the conversions were so late that Google was basically bidding blind for two days.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: We moved that campaign to manual bidding as a a stopgap.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Which campaign was that?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The fall tune-up one. It's not huge, maybe 8% of our spend, but we don't want to run manual forever.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And the bigger issue is we can't trust the conversion numbers when we're looking at week-over-week performance. [PERSON_2] spends half her day reconciling.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, I've been exporting from Invoca and from Google and matching them up manually. It's not sustainable.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. So two things: the delay itself, and the manual work it's creating. Let me ask a couple of questions.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: When did you first notice it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'd say the first week of August. I flagged it to our Google rep, and they said it's on the Invoca side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. And is it all conversions or specific ones? Like, are the appointment booked signals coming through faster than the quote given ones?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It's all of them. I checked. Even the ones that should be near real-time.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. And have you changed anything in the integration setup? New tracking numbers, new campaigns?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No, nothing on our end. Like, we added a couple of new numbers for the fall campaign, but the delay started before that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And we're not doing anything weird with the data. It's the same fields we've always sent.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. I'm going to take this back to our integrations team. I don't want to guess at a cause. Can you send me a couple of examples?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Call IDs and the timestamps when they hit Google?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, I can pull that together. I have a spreadsheet already.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. And if you can include the campaign and the GCLID, that would help them trace it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Will do. I'll send it by end of day Monday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Great. I'll open a ticket and loop you like, in. In the meantime, is there anything else on the Google side that's acting up?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, the rest is fine. The call tracking and the signals are working like they should.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. And how's the team holding up? I know you mentioned you were down a person.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, we lost our paid search manager in July. We're interviewing, but it's slow. [PERSON_2]'s been covering.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It's I mean, fine. I just don't have time for manual reconciliation, which is why this is bugging me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Totally fair. Let me also check on the Meta side while I'm at it. Are those conversions coming through on time?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Meta looks normal. It's just Google.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. So I'll focus on Google. Anything else before we wrap?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that's the the main thing. We just need it fixed before Q4 um, planning.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. I'll get the ticket going today and follow up with the team. And [PERSON_2], send those examples when you can.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Will do. Thanks, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks, both. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Bye.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], hey [PERSON_2]. Thanks for making time. How's the week going over there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Pretty good. Busy. We're heading into the fall pest season so the phones are starting to pick up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, it's that time. We usually see a jump in ant and rodent calls around now.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Makes sense. I pulled the numbers before this. You had about 1,400 calls last month across the six locations, up maybe 9 percent from July.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Does that track with what you're seeing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That sounds about right. August was strong. We're hoping September holds.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Raleigh and Cary are carrying most of it. The Wilmington office is still slow.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. [PERSON_2], I know you run all of this yourself. Anything on your list you want to walk through today?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: A few things. First, the Google Ads side is fine. The offline conversions are landing and we can see them in the campaigns.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good to hear. And the signal setup, appointment booked and quote given, still tagging the way you want?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, those are working. We tweaked the quote signal in July so it catches the estimate calls and that helped.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That was a good fix. Less junk in the report.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Nice. So what's on your mind?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I'll jump in. This is more of a wish than a problem. Every Monday [PERSON_2] pulls the call report out as a CSV and then she's the one pasting it into a Google Sheet for me and the branch managers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It's not hard, but it's a chore. And then [PERSON_1] wants it sliced by location, so I'm doing pivot tables before I've had coffee.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: What I'd really like is for that dashboard to just show up. In Looker, or a Google Sheet, or whatever BI tool, on a schedule.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So Monday morning it's there and nobody's copying and pasting.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So the ask is a way to push dashboard metrics out on a schedule, rather than exporting the file by hand.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Right. And honestly if there were an API endpoint for the dashboard numbers, I've got a guy who could wire it into Looker and we'd never touch it again.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. Let me write that down. So scheduled delivery, and an endpoint for the metrics. Which numbers matter most to you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Calls by location, calls by campaign, and how many turned into booked appointments. That's the three I look at.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. I'll take that back to the product team and see what's possible. I can't promise anything on timing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yep, understood.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: One other thing, totally separate. We hired two new CSRs in Raleigh, so I need to get them set up as users.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Can you point me to the steps?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Sure, I'll email you the invite flow after this. Takes about five minutes per seat.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Perfect.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: How's everything else holding up? Tracking numbers, the dynamic number insertion on the site?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Fine. No issues there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hey, did you all get that storm last night? Power blinked here twice.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Just rain on my side of town. My dog was not thrilled about it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Ha. Same here.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, so I'll follow up on the scheduled reporting ask and send the user setup steps. Anything else before we hop off?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's it from us. Thanks [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Appreciate it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks both. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], how's it going?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_2]. Doing alright, busy Monday. How about you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Same here. I've got a few accounts stacked up this afternoon, so this is a nice break. Anything new on your end before we get into it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Mostly the usual. We're at about 4,100 calls across the seven stores this month, which is up maybe 6 percent from August. The Tulsa and Broken Arrow stores are carrying most of it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That tracks with what I saw when I pulled the account earlier. Are you still running the same tracking numbers per campaign, or did anything shift when the new GM came in?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Numbers are the same. But that's kind of why I wanted to talk today. There's something the team keeps running into.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So the offline call conversions we push to Google Ads, they're landing one to three days after the call. We're feeding Smart Bidding data that's already stale, and it's making the bid decisions worse, not better.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: One to three days. Is that consistent, or does it bounce around?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It bounces. Some come through same day, but a lot of them sit for two or three days. Our BDC is logging outcomes in Salesforce same day, so the delay isn't on our side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And you're seeing this across all campaigns or just certain ones?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Mostly the ones with higher volume. The Fort Smith store's lead gen campaign is the worst. We actually moved that one to manual bidding last week just to stop the bleeding.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, so manual bidding is the stopgap for now. Who made that call?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I did. The new GM, Roger, wasn't thrilled about it, but he understood. He's been asking a lot of questions about the whole setup since he started in August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's fair. New GM, new set of eyes. How's he settling in?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: He's alright. Sharp guy. He came from a group down in Texas, so he's used to a different stack. He's been looking at Marchex, mostly comparing pricing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Understood. I'm not going to get into a comparison today, but I'd like to understand what's driving that. Is it the billing, the reporting, something else?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Honestly, the bidding thing is part of it. If our conversions aren't flowing fast enough, it makes the whole platform look like it's not pulling its weight.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That makes sense. Let me ask a couple of things so I can take this back to the right people. When did you first notice the lag?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Probably three or four weeks ago. It got worse when we bumped up spend in September.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. And is this only on the Google Ads side, or are you seeing it in Salesforce too?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Salesforce is fine. Leads are showing up same day. It's just the conversion push to Google.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. I want to get the specific campaign IDs and a couple of call examples where the delay was longest. Can you send those over?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, I can pull that together. Probably by tomorrow morning.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Perfect. I'll open this up on my end and get it in front of the team that owns the Google Ads integration. I can't promise a fix timeline today, but I'll make sure it's in the queue with the right priority.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Appreciate that. One other thing, and this is minor. We're down a BDC rep in Oklahoma City, so call handling there is thin. If you see a dip in answered rates, that's why.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good to know. Do you want me to keep an eye on that store specifically for the next few weeks?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That'd help. Just so we don't get surprised at month end.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Done. Anything else on the Signal AI side while we're here?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that's been fine. The appointment booked signal is still matching up with what the BDC logs, so no complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. I'll leave that alone then. Let me get the ticket going today and I'll follow up with you Thursday or Friday once I have an update.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thursday works. I'll have the campaign list to you in the morning.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Sounds good. Hey, before I let you go, are you still doing the Friday ride-alongs with the sales team?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Every other week. It's the only way I get out of the office. Roger's actually tagging along this Friday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Nice. Good luck with that. Talk Thursday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks [PERSON_2]. Talk then.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Morning, [PERSON_1]. How's the week going over there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Morning, [PERSON_2]. Busy. Storm season, so claims are up. We're at about 4,100 calls a day through Genesys, which is a good 20 percent over August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That tracks with what I saw in the volume dashboard. Are you holding up on staffing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Barely. We pulled four people off the auto team onto claims intake. [PERSON_3] is running the schedule and she's basically begging for overtime approvals.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. And how's the after-hours pilot going? That was the thing I most wanted to hear about.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's early, but the AI Voice Agent is picking up maybe 60 percent of the calls that used to hit voicemail, so that's the win we wanted. No complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. Anything on PreSense or QM you want to flag while I've got you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Actually, yeah, there is one thing, and it's been biting us for a couple weeks.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So when a call gets transferred in Genesys, either queue to queue or agent to agent, the screen pop comes up blank for whoever picks it up. The original agent sees everything fine. The receiving agent gets nothing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Blank as in no PreSense data at all, or blank as in fields showing empty?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No PreSense data. No pages viewed, no campaign, nothing. The agent has to ask the caller everything again from scratch.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: How often are we talking?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's the thing. I had my team pull last Tuesday's transfers. We counted 84 transfers across the day, and 71 of them came in blank. So yeah, it's high. Call it 85 percent of transfers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Seventy-one of eighty-four. Okay, that's not a rounding error, that's most of them.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Right. And it's worse on the home side. Auto transfers seem to come through maybe half the time, but home is almost always empty.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Interesting. Does it matter whether it's a warm transfer with the agent still on the line versus a straight queue transfer?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I don't have that broken out. I can get you that if it helps.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It would. And one more, when did you first notice it? Anything change around then?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Early September, I think. I don't know of anything we changed on our end. Genesys config has been stable since June.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. I'm going to write this up and get it in front of our support team this morning, with the transfer counts and the Genesys details. Can you send me that Tuesday report, even if it's just a spreadsheet?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, I'll have [PERSON_3] send it over today.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Perfect. And [PERSON_1], I'm not going to guess at a fix on the call, I just want the team to have the specifics.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Understood. I mostly want to know if it's us or you, honestly.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Fair. I'll push for a clear answer on that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Appreciate it. Oh, and one small thing, our Adobe Analytics numbers for August look right, so no worries on that side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good to hear. How about the Google Ads side? Still sending conversions?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Far as I know, yes. Nobody's said otherwise.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. One more logistics thing, QM scorecards. You're still on the same set from July, right?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yes, no changes. The adjusters seem happy with them. Or at least nobody's complained to me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll take that. Do you want to do the QM review as part of our next call, or separately?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Separately, if we can. The next check-in is already going to be crowded if this transfer thing is still open.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Makes sense. I'll send a separate invite for the first week of October. Same time?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Tuesday works. Not the 6th, I'm out that day.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Noted. I'll do the 7th at 9:30, unless I hear otherwise.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: One tangent, did your team end up using the AI Messaging Agent on the abandoned quote follow-ups?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We turned it on for a small group in August. It's been fine, nothing to report. [PERSON_4] ran it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Great. I'll leave that alone then.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, focus on the transfer thing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Will do. So to recap on my side, I'm filing the PreSense blank screen pop today with your transfer counts, waiting on the Tuesday spreadsheet from [PERSON_3], and scheduling the QM review for the 7th. Anything else before I let you go?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that covers it. Thanks, [PERSON_2].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thanks, [PERSON_1]. Hang in there with the storm volume.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We'll survive. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hi [PERSON_1], thanks for making the time. How's the week going over there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Busy. We're down two people on the member care floor, so everyone's picking up extra shifts.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's a lot. Is that temporary coverage or are you hiring for those seats?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hiring, but you know how it goes. Interviews take forever in our HR process. Should be filled by November, hopefully.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. I pulled the numbers before this call so we could walk through them together. Last quarter Harbor had about 61,000 inbound calls across all campaigns.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Does that match what you're seeing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Roughly. I think we were closer to 63,000 if you count the overflow line for the loan team.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, I'll check whether that number is pulling into the same campaign group. And the Google Ads side, you're still sending conversions back for the Smart Bidding campaigns?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yes, that's still running the way it was. We haven't touched it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. How about Salesforce? Any changes on the Financial Services Cloud side since we talked in June?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, same setup. Call records land on the member record like before.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. Let me switch to the quality management piece, since that's what we set aside most of the hour for.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yes, please. That's the part I actually wanted to talk through.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Tell me what's been coming up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So our QA team has a rubric they've used for years, before we ever had software scoring calls. It has specific things they listen for on each call type.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: A HELOC inquiry has different checkpoints than a fraud report or a card dispute. Right now the scorecard in the platform doesn't map to any of that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: When you say specific checkpoints, what kinds of things?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Exact disclosures. Reg Z language on lending calls, the fraud liability script, the identity verification steps. Word for word matters to us, not just the gist of it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: If an agent paraphrases, that's a finding in our rubric.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And the scoring today doesn't let you build that granularity in?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not at the level we need. We'd want to define the criteria ourselves, per call type, and weight them. The identity verification piece should carry more weight on a fraud call than it does on a general servicing question.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Right now everything's scored the same way across the board and our compliance reviews come back asking why the scores don't line up with what the QA team would have given.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So the ask is essentially: let Harbor build scorecards that mirror your existing rubric, with call-type specific questions and weighting.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's it exactly. If the platform's scoring lined up with the rubric my team already uses, we wouldn't have to run two parallel QA processes.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And our compliance reviews would get simpler because there'd be one number instead of two.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: How often does compliance review the scorecards today?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Every time we change one. Our internal audit group signs off on any scoring change before it goes live, so we've been pretty conservative about what we adjust.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Understood. I'm going to write this up for our product team with the examples you gave, Reg Z, fraud liability, identity verification, and the weighting piece.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Can I use Harbor's name in that write-up, or do you want it anonymized?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: You can use our name. No issue there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Great. I can't promise a timeline from here, but I'll get it in front of the right people and let you know what I hear back.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Anything else on the QA side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that's the one. Everything else on that end is working the way we expect.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. Last thing from my side, your renewal comes up in February 2027. We don't need to do anything now, but I'll start the internal prep on that after the first of the year so it's not a scramble.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That works. I'll be on leave the first two weeks of January, so maybe aim for the back half of the month.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Noted, back half of January. Do you want me to send a recap of today with the numbers and the scorecard request?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yes, send it to me and I'll forward it to my director.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Will do, probably this afternoon. Thanks for the time, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks, [PERSON_2]. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], hey [PERSON_2]. Thanks for making time this afternoon. I know things have been busy on your side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hi [PERSON_3]. Yeah, it's been a week. [PERSON_2]'s joining because he's been hearing about this from his supervisors too.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Morning, [PERSON_3]. Or afternoon for you. Let's just get into it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Of course. So I have the two escalations from earlier this quarter in my notes. Want to start with what's happening now, or walk me through the history first?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Let's do now. The issue is when Genesys transfers a call between queues or from one agent to another, the PreSense screen pop comes up blank for whoever receives it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Blank meaning no digital journey data at all, or blank meaning the fields are there but empty?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Completely blank. White panel. The agent sees the caller's number and that's it. No pages viewed, no ad source, nothing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And this isn't every transfer. [PERSON_1], what's the rough rate?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We tracked it for two weeks. About one in five transfers. So if a rep takes forty transferred calls a day, eight of them are flying blind.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. And the first agent, the one who originally answered, they see the pop fine?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: First agent is fine. It's only after the transfer fires. That's what makes it so frustrating, because the receiving agent is usually the one who needs the context most.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. When did you first notice it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Middle of July. We raised it with support, they asked for examples, we sent a batch. Then it went quiet for a few weeks and it came back in August, so we raised it again.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And that's why I'm on the call. My supervisors are escalating it internally. They're the ones hearing it from the floor every day.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's fair. Can you tell me which queues are involved? Is it specific ones or all of them?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sales primarily. New activations and upgrades. We did see it once in retention but that was a single call, so I don't want to overstate it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. And the transfer, is it always agent to agent, or does it also happen when the IVR routes to a queue?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Agent to agent mostly. The queue transfers are less common but I've seen a couple.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. What I'd like to do is get a few call IDs where the receiving agent saw the blank pop, plus the timestamps and the Genesys transfer events if you can pull them.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That'll let my team line up the PreSense delivery against the transfer.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: How many do you need?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Ten would be plenty. If you can get me ten from different days, that's better than fifty from one afternoon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I can get you ten by Thursday. I'll have my lead pull them from the Genesys reporting side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. And I'll open a case with our engineering team today and reference the two earlier tickets so they see the pattern.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Appreciate that. One thing I want to flag, [PERSON_3]. We're not asking for a fix on this call. We just need to know it's being looked at seriously.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I hear that. I can't give you a date today, but I can commit to a status update by end of next week, even if the update is just where it sits.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That would help. The silence in August was worse than the bug, honestly.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Noted. I'll own the updates. Now, separate topic, how are call volumes looking this month?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Up. We're averaging around 61,000 calls a month across all campaigns, which is about nine percent over August. Back to school promo is doing a lot of that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Nice. Any change on the Google Ads side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that's been steady. Offline conversions are flowing. Adobe Analytics is fine too.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. And how's the AI Voice Agent handling the after-hours queue?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's fine. Same as last quarter. No complaints from the team.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: We did add six reps to the sales floor in September, so the transfer volume is only going up from here.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's useful context. More transfers means more chances for this to show up, so the timing matters.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Exactly. And we're heading into Q4 hiring, so it's not going to slow down.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Let me recap what I'm taking away. Ten call examples by Thursday, I open the case today, and you get a status from me by end of next week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That works.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Same. Thanks for getting on this, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks both. [PERSON_1], send those IDs straight to me and I'll confirm when the case is in. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Will do. Bye.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Take care.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], good to hear your voice. How's Wednesday treating you down in Tampa?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_2]. Not bad. Busy week, we're prepping for the fall promo push, but I can't complain.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Nice. I saw the call volume ticked up last week. You all holding up okay on staffing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, we're getting by. We had two folks out on PTO, so the queue got a little backed up Tuesday afternoon, but the team caught up by Wednesday morning.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. Anything you need from me on the routing side while you're shorthanded?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not right now. The Amazon Connect flows are doing their job. But I do want to flag something about the AI Voice Agent that's been nagging at us.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So when the voice agent hands a call off to a live person, the stuff it already collected from the caller doesn't come through with the transfer.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: The caller tells the bot their order number, their name, what they need, and then my agent picks up and has to ask all over again.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Does that happen on every transfer, or only certain call types?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Seems like most of them. Store hours and order status calls that get escalated, the context just drops. And the callers notice.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: You can hear the frustration in their voice when they have to repeat themselves.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: How long has this been going on?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: A few weeks now. I didn't escalate it right away because we were in the middle of the showroom rollout for the new mattress line.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: But it's showing up in our numbers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Which numbers?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: CSAT on transferred calls is running lower than on the calls the AI handles end to end. Not a huge gap, but it's consistent.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And my team is spending extra time on those calls because they're basically starting from scratch.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. I want to get this in front of the right folks. Do you have a recent call ID or two where it happened?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I can pull a couple. I'll send them over after this call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Perfect. And is it affecting any specific showroom more than others, or is it across the board?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Across the board, as far as I can tell. It's not tied to one location.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Understood. I'll take this back to the product team and see what they need from us. I can't promise a timeline, but I'll keep you posted.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's all I ask. Appreciate it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Of course. Switching gears, how's the PreSense screen pop working for your agents?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's fine. No complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. And the Google Ads and Meta conversions are still flowing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, no issues. My marketing counterpart checks them weekly.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Great. One housekeeping thing: I'll be out the first week of October, so if anything urgent comes up, my teammate can step in.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll send an intro email.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sounds good. I'll keep an eye out.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Alright, I'll follow up once I hear back from the team. Thanks for the detail, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks, [PERSON_2]. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Morning, [PERSON_1]. Morning, [PERSON_2]. How's Phoenix treating you? Still hot?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, we're in that fake fall window. Ninety-eight yesterday, supposed to be a hundred and one tomorrow.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Uh, I was in Vegas Monday and Tuesday. Same thing. The AC in the Henderson store went out, so I spent most of Tuesday in a conference room there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Oh man. Did it get fixed?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Wednesday morning. The tech was there at seven. Um, it was fine, just a compressor thing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay so, agenda-wise, [PERSON_3], I know you had a couple of uh, things.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah, mostly logistics. Let me pull up my notes here. You know, Um, one thing I wanted to check on is the Q4 training dates.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I know we talked about getting the BDC folks on a refresher before the holiday push.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Right. So that's [PERSON_2]'s area more than mine.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I mean, yeah. We've got about forty people in the BDC across the rooftops. What were the dates you were thinking?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I had two windows held. First is October 14th and 15th, second is the 21st and 22nd. Um, Both are Tuesdays like, and Wednesdays, two hours each morning.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The 14th and and 15th is better. The 21st we've got a regional managers meeting in Tucson, so half the room would be on a laptop in a hotel.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, let's lock the 14th and 15th. Do you want me to send the calendar holds to you and [PERSON_1], or should I go straight to the BDC leads?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Send to me first. I'll forward. There's a couple of new team leads I want to make sure actually show up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. And is it still the same group of forty, or has that changed?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It's thirty-eight now. Two people moved over to the service side in August. And we picked up one at the Scottsdale store, so, you know, net minus one.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sorry, hold on. [PERSON_2], was that the the Scottsdale BDC hire, the one that started Labor Day week?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah. You know, she came over from the internet sales desk there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay. I just wanted to make sure I wasn't double counting her.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Um, no problem. I'll put thirty-eight on the invite and we can adjust. Um, the other thing, user changes. I got a ticket that one of your marketing coordinators left in early September?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, that's right. Her last day was the 11th. You know, we haven't backfilled yet. Probably posting it next week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Do you want me to deactivate her access now, or leave it until the replacement starts?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Deactivate now. [PERSON_2] can tell you, we're pretty strict about that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, please do. Finance gets twitchy about active accounts with no owner.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Makes sense. Um, I'll do that today and send you a confirmation.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Appreciate it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Last one from me, and this is just me being nosy about planning. What does your call volume look like heading into October?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'm trying to get ahead of any support coverage gaps on my side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Historically we see um, a bump the second week of October, then it flattens until Black Friday. Last year October was up, what, eleven percent over September?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Somewhere in there. I'd have to pull the actual number.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Don't hold me to eleven. It was a real bump, that's all I remember.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's helpful enough. I mean, I'll just make sure my coverage is normal through that stretch.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And the holiday hours kick in the week of Thanksgiving, so the BDC schedule shifts. I'll send you that once it's final.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. Anything from you two before we wrap?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Nope, I think we're good. Everything on our end is just steady. Thanks for the training dates.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Same. Thanks, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Great. I'll send the invite today and the deactivation confirmation. Talk to you both in a couple weeks. Stay cool out there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Ha. We'll try.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hi both, thanks for making the time. How's everything on your end?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Pretty good. Busy season is starting to ramp, so the timing works.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Same here. I was just pulling some numbers before this, actually.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Perfect. I figured we'd do a quick pass on how things are running, and then I want to hear about the after-hours pilot.

turns.text: Okay, so, agenda. You sent a couple of things over.

turns.text: Yeah. I mostly wanted to check in on the voice agent numbers and whatever [PERSON_2]'s got running, and then look at where we are before the fall push.

turns.text: Before we get into that, one thing I want to put on I mean, the record, because I've been meaning to send it up to you you.

turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So, our website's one of those single-page apps, right? When somebody taps a phone number on a showroom page, the page doesn't do a full reload, it swaps the content underneath.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And what we're seeing is the number doesn't swap with it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Meaning the dynamic number insertion isn't firing on the route change.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Right. So a customer on the mobile site, they click to call, and they're getting the default number, not the one tied to whatever page or campaign brought them in.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It's not every call, but it's enough that I don't trust the attribution on mobile anymore.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I mean, okay. How long do you figure this has been going on?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Honestly? Probably since the site rebuild over the like, summer. Nobody flagged it until my team lead on the queue started comparing call logs to the ad reports and the numbers didn't line up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And I care about so, this because if mobile click-to-call isn't attributing, then Google Ads is getting fed garbage, and I'm making budget calls off garbage.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: No, that makes sense. Let me ask a couple of things so I can describe it accurately when I bring it to to the team.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Is it happening on both iOS and Android, or did you only test one?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: We saw it on both. My analyst pulled a sample last week, I want to say around nine hundred mobile sessions, and about forty of them showed the wrong number in the source.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. And is it just the showroom pages or also the campaign landing pages?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Both, I think. The landing pages are simpler so it's harder to to catch, but yeah.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. I'm not going to guess at what's behind it. Let me write it up with those details and get it in front of the right folks, and I'll come back to you with questions rather than a theory.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's you know, all I'm asking. Put it in writing so I've got something to point at.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Will do. Okay, other side of the house. How's the voice agent doing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. It's handling store hours and order status, those two intents, and it's taking a real bite out of the queue.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Last month it was, what, about a third of inbound?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thirty-four percent, yeah. And on Sundays it's higher because we run lean.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And the transfers to live agents, are those landing where you want them?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: They are. Amazon Connect's been solid. Had to move one supervisor to a later shift because the call curve shifted, but that's a staffing thing, not a system thing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Speak for yourself, I'm still fighting for that headcount.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: You and me um, both.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Anything else that's come up that you want me to carry back?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No. Everything else we're running is fine. This is the one that's bugging me.

turns.text: Same. We're heads down on Q4, so I don't have bandwidth for a project right now anyway.

turns.text: Understood. So what I'll do, I'll get the write-up together today or tomorrow, and copy you both so you can add anything I missed.

turns.text: So you're scoring the calls but not that particular behavior.

turns.text: How many HELOC calls a week are we talking?

turns.text: And it's the same disclosure every time, or does it vary by call type?

turns.text: We're adding a second Spanish-language queue in November. That's the big one. I'll need to think about how that affects scoring, but that's a next-year problem.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: All of it. They took last year's invoice and this year's and went line by line, and the add-on lines are the ones they circled.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: How much of that is procurement versus you and [PERSON_2]?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's mostly procurement. But they ask me why the seller experience we promised needs a separate line, and I don't have a good answer for them.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And I'll be honest with you, [PERSON_3]. We've started taking calls from other vendors because of this.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. I want to make sure I understand the shape of it before I take it anywhere. [PERSON_2], when you say other vendors, are those exploratory conversations or something further along?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Exploratory. Nobody's sent us a proposal. But the add-on pricing friction at renewal is tied to whether we even get to a proposal stage with anyone.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's clear. I'm not going to sit here and promise anything on the pricing structure today. What I can do is get the specifics in front of the people who own it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's all I'm asking. I need something concrete before we start building the FY27 budget in December.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. Can you send me the two invoices, marked up the way procurement did it? That way I'm not paraphrasing when I take it back.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll get that to you by Monday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And [PERSON_3], on the day-to-day, everything's working. Signal AI is tagging the way it should, transcripts look right. This is a money conversation, not a product one.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good to know. I'll come back to you both next week with what I hear. Thanks for being direct about it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks, [PERSON_3]. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Bye, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hi [PERSON_1], hi [PERSON_2]. Thanks for making the time. I know this was short notice on our side, so I appreciate you both jumping on.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Sure, [PERSON_3]. [PERSON_1] filled me in a bit, but I want to hear it from you too.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah. So, we've got a problem with Signal AI that I need to escalate. It's the spam detection.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Tell me what you're seeing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We pulled a sample of calls that Signal AI tagged as spam over the last three weeks. About 180 calls. We listened to them.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Most of those were real customers. People calling Saturday morning about a claim, or after hours on a Sunday. Not spam at all.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So legitimate after-hours and weekend callers are getting flagged as spam and dropping out of reporting.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Right. Which means our weekend claims volume looks lower than it actually is. And some of those calls aren't getting followed up the way they should.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's the part that worries me. If a homeowner calls Saturday about water damage and we've filed it as junk, that's a coverage conversation waiting to happen.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: [PERSON_2], that's fair. How many of the 180 did you get through?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We listened to all of them. Maybe 140, 150 were real. The rest were actual junk, robocalls, a couple of wrong numbers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And was this recent, or has it been going on longer?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It got worse around Labor Day weekend. Before that it was maybe a handful a week. Now it's dozens.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. And are these coming through the main claims line, or the after-hours flow?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Mostly after-hours and weekend. When the AI Voice Agent picks up and then transfers to a live adjuster.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. So the transfer calls specifically.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's where we see the concentration, yeah.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. I want to get the call IDs and a couple of the ones you listened to. Can you send me the list, or should I pull it from the reporting side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I can send you the spreadsheet. It has the call IDs and the timestamps.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. I'll take this to the Signal AI team today and come back to you with what they find. I'm not going to guess at a cause on the call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: How long are we talking? Because if this keeps happening through the winter storm season, I need to know.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll push for an update by next Wednesday. If I don't have an answer by then, I'll tell you where it stands.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That works.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: While I have you, how's the Genesys side holding up? Any routing issues?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Genesys is fine. The PreSense screen pops are doing what they should. No complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. And the AI Voice Agent pilot? Still after-hours claims only?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Still after-hours claims. We're keeping it contained until we see a full quarter.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Makes sense. What's the volume looking like?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: About 40, 45 calls a night on the agent, and most of those transfer to a live person. We're adding two adjusters to the overnight shift next month to keep up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Noted. I'll keep that in mind when we plan the next review.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: [PERSON_1], did you want to mention the QM scorecard calibration?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Oh, right. That's separate. We're doing a scorecard calibration session in two weeks. Nothing urgent, just scheduling.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I can send over a few times for that. Does the week of the 19th work?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I think so. I'll check with the team.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: One other thing, [PERSON_3]. My daughter's college tour is in Columbus next Friday, so I may be late to our monthly.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: [PERSON_1] can start without me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: No problem at all. [PERSON_1], I'll send the calendar invite for the monthly and the calibration options this afternoon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Great.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And I'll follow up on the Signal AI issue by Wednesday. If anything changes on your end before then, just email me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thanks, [PERSON_3]. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks. Bye.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. How are you feeling about it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Honestly, I don't know enough about the sync timing to judge. We run Google Ads hard for new patients, and if their conversion data lands faster than ours, that's a real question for how our bidding behaves.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's fair. Can I ask what your current sync timing looks like on your end, just so I understand where you're starting from?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I'd have to check with the person who set it up originally. I think it's been the same since we launched, and nobody's really touched it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. Let me ask our team what the sync timing looks like for an account like yours, and I'll get you a straight answer. I don't want to guess at it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That would help. And I'm not in a rush to switch. It's more that I don't want to get caught flat-footed if they're genuinely ahead on something.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Understood. I'll come back to you with specifics, and if it makes sense we can look at it together. Anything else on your list?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: One small thing. We're adding a Saturday morning slot at the Eagle office starting in November, so call routing may look different on weekends. Do I need to tell anyone on your side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: If you're using the same tracking numbers, probably not. But send me the details and I'll double check nothing needs adjusting.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Will do. Oh, and [PERSON_3] asked me to say hi. She's still running the front desk at the downtown office.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Tell her hi back. Is she still doing the Tuesday huddle with the other managers?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: She is. It's turned into a nice little ritual, they go over the week's calls and compare notes.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's great to hear. Anything on the Signal side you want to flag while we're here?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that's all been fine. Appointment booked and quote given are the two we lean on, and they're working the way they always have.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. I'll follow up on the sync question early next week. That work for you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Tuesday or Wednesday is better, I'm out Monday for a school thing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Noted. I'll send it Tuesday. Have a good weekend, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: You too, [PERSON_2]. Thanks.
