turns.text: Coastal Comfort Mattress escalation Mon, Oct 5, 2026, 8:45AM • 3:39

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:03 Morning, [PERSON_2]. How's Tampa treating you? Still humid?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:07 Oh, you you know, it's October and it's still ninety degrees. I'm over it.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:13 Ha. Like, yeah, I've got the AC running at home still. Anyway, so, what's going on?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:20 So, uh, this is kind of why I wanted to get on the phone. We've so, had something come up with the voice agent that I think is, um, pretty urgent.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:35 Okay, tell me.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:37 When the AI Voice Agent transfers a caller to one of our live folks in Amazon Connect, the stuff it collected doesn't come through. So the agent picks up and has no idea what the caller already told the bot. They have to start over. Name, order number, all of it.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:57 So the transfer note is coming in blank, basically.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:01 Blank. Yeah. And I'll give you an example. Saturday morning, a lady called about a delivery window, spent, I I want to say a minute and a half with the agent, gave her order number, her zip, everything. Transfers over. And our person in the call center asks her for the order number again. She was... she was not happy.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:23 Yikes. How long has this been happening?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:26 Honestly, we think a couple of weeks. It got noticed because, you know, the agents started complaining. Our team lead over in the call center, [PERSON_3], she's the one who flagged it. She pulled a few recordings and showed me.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:44 Okay. And is it every transfer, or is it specific to certain call types? Like order status versus store hours?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:52 That's the thing, we're not totally sure. It seems like most of them. Like, the store-hours ones usually don't transfer, so...

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:59 Right, yeah. So it's the order-status and delivery ones you know, mostly.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:05 Mostly, yeah. I don't have a a clean count yet. I can get you you a list of examples if that helps.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:13 That would help a lot, yeah. Dates, like, times, maybe the caller's number for a couple of them, so we can pull the recordings on our side.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:23 Okay. I can probably get that to you by tomorrow. I've got a showroom walkthrough this afternoon in Sarasota, so it might be end of day.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:34 No rush, tomorrow's fine. Let me get this in front of our support team today and I'll own the follow-up. Can I use you as the contact?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:44 Yeah, me or [PERSON_3]. Either like, one.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:47 Perfect. Separately, real quick, your call volume's been trending up, right? I saw we're past 11,000 a month now.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:56 Yeah, we added four showrooms since spring, so that tracks. We're hiring two more in the call center just to keep up.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:05 Good problem to have. And the Google Ads side, that's all fine?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 3:10 Fine as far as I know. Nothing new there.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:14 Okay. Alright, so I'll log this, loop in support, and come back to you once I've got a a case number and a next step. Probably by end of day.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 3:27 That works. Thanks, [PERSON_1]. And hey, sorry to start your Monday with this.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:33 It's what I'm here for. Go enjoy Sarasota. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Coastal Comfort Mattress QBR Mon, Oct 5, 2026, 9:00AM • 4:46

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:02 Morning, both. How's the weather down in Tampa? I saw there was some rain over the weekend.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:10 Oh, it it dumped. My drive in you know, this morning was basically a boat ride. But it's cleared up now.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 0:19 Yeah, our store in [PERSON_4] had water coming in near the loading dock. Nothing serious, just a mop situation.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:26 Glad it wasn't worse. Okay, so we've got the QBR today. I want to spend most of the time on the AI Voice Agent, since that's the newest piece, and then look at the rest of the account. Does that work?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:45 Works for me. [PERSON_3]'s got the numbers pulled.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:48 Uh, Perfect. [PERSON_3], walk me through it.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 0:51 Sure. So for September, total inbound across all 64 showrooms was about 41,200 calls. That's up from 38,600 in August. Tracking numbers are live on every campaign, DNI is working on the site.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:06 And how much of that hit the voice agent?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 1:10 Roughly 11,400. Store hours and order status, mostly. About 62 percent of those resolved without a transfer to a live agent.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:19 That's solid. Is the transfer rate holding where you want it?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:24 It's fine. We're not worried about it.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:28 Good. And Amazon Connect, any changes on your side?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 1:32 No, same setup. We did add six seats in the contact center in September, so we're at 55 now.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:41 Noted. I'll make sure the seat count is right on our end before renewal.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 1:47 Renewal's not till August, right?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:50 August 15th, yeah. Plenty of runway.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:53 Okay, so, there's one thing I want to bring up while we have you. It's not urgent, but it keeps coming uh, up on my side.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:04 Go ahead.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:06 Every Monday morning, [PERSON_3] sits down and exports CSVs out of the platform by hand. Call volumes by showroom, by campaign, a couple of other cuts. Then she loads them into Looker for the regional directors.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 2:22 And into a Google Sheet for the store managers, because they don't have Looker access. So it's two places every week.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:29 How long does that take you?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 2:32 If nothing breaks, maybe an hour and a half. Last Monday it was closer to three because one like, of the exports timed out and I had to redo it.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:44 And it's the same six or seven reports every week. So what I'd love, and I know I'm not the only one asking, is for those to just land in Looker, or Sheets, or whatever BI tool, on a schedule. Push, not pull. [PERSON_3] shouldn't be the integration.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:06 So scheduled delivery into Looker and so, Google Sheets, and probably other BI tools too, so nobody's hand-exporting.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 3:12 Right. Same reports, same schedule, every Monday at seven.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:16 Got it. Is it the same report definitions each week, or does the list change?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 3:23 Same ones. Occasionally I add a column, but the reports themselves don't change.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:29 Okay. Let me write this up and take it to the product team. I can't tell you what they'll say or when, but I'll come back to you you with an answer either way.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 3:44 That's all I'm asking.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:46 Anything else on the reporting side, or is that the one?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 3:52 That's the one.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:54 Okay. Switching gears, Google Ads offline conversions. Are those still matching the way they should?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 4:01 Yep, no issues there. Meta's the same.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:04 Good. Anything you want me to look at before the next check-in?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 4:10 I don't think so. Oh, one scheduling thing. Can we move the next one earlier? I mean, First week of December gets messy with holiday staffing.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:23 Sure. I'll send options for the week of November 16th. [PERSON_3], you're on that too?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 4:29 I'll be there.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:31 Great. I'll get the recap out this afternoon with the reporting ask in writing so it's documented.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 4:38 Perfect. Thanks, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:41 Thanks both. Stay dry down there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: You know, Morning [PERSON_1]. How's the weather treating you up in Hartford?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Oh, you know. Fifty-two and drizzling. I'll take it over the snow that's coming.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Ha, fair. So I've got um, the QBR deck up. Want to start with volumes, or do you want to just talk?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Let's just talk. Uh, the deck stuff I can read later. Honestly the thing on my mind is the QM rollout.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So, okay. Where are you sitting on seats?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Um, Seventy-one of the hundred and thirty licensed, so we're behind where I wanted. [PERSON_3] has been out since the the end of August, and she was running the live trainings for the Hartford floor.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Right, you mentioned that. Is she back yet?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Back next Monday, so I'm hoping we finish the remaining fifty-nine by end of month. And the scoring's been fine, people are getting used to it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. Anything else in the platform giving you trouble?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that part's okay. The thing I keep running into is the scorecards themselves.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Tell me more.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So we're scoring a Medicare Advantage call differently than a P&C quote call, obviously. Right now I'm working inside the criteria that are there, and it's a lot of bending.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I want to be able to build my own criteria.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Like define new questions from scratch?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, and attach them to the call type, so a MA call gets the MA set and a P&C call doesn't.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And let me weight things.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Weighting meaning some criteria count more toward the score?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Exactly. Right now if an agent um, reads the required disclosure language, that's the same as them saying the greeting. Those aren't the same thing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, that's clear. Is it the disclosure piece that's most uh, urgent?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's the one that keeps me up. Um, I need to verify the exact required language verbatim, and I don't want to fold that into a generic criteria and hope.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. Let me write this down so I bring it back right. Custom criteria, so, call-type-specific um, scoring, weighting, and the disclosure check.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's it. I'm not asking for it tomorrow, I just want it on the radar.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll take it to the QM product folks and see what's possible. No promises on timing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Fine by me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, quickly on the numbers. September was about 41,200 calls across the network, up maybe four percent from August. Google Ads conversions still flowing through with the GCLID matching, Salesforce is writing the call records the way your ops team wanted.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good. PreSense screen pops have been solid for the Genesys agents, the journey info shows up before they answer. No complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Glad to hear it. Uh, Anything you need from me before the next one?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Just the scorecard thing. And say hi to your dog for me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Like, Ha, will do. I'll send notes by Wednesday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sounds good. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Morning, both. How's Austin treating you? Still stupid hot?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Man, it was 97 on Saturday. In October. My kid's soccer game, we we were all just melting on the sideline.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And Phoenix is worse. My counterpart over there keeps sending me screenshots of his uh, car thermometer like it's a competition.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Um, Ha. Okay, so, what I wanted to do today is just a check-in. Volumes, anything on your end, and I know you flagged something on the agents.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: How'd September land?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: September was strong. We did about 41,000 inbound across the three states, which is up maybe 12 percent over August. Google Ads is still carrying most of it, Meta's been softer since the middle of the month.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Softer is generous. The Meta leads, the quality just isn't there right now. But the Google side, yeah, we're getting good volume.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Got it. And the floor, are you fully staffed? I remember you were down a couple of Spanish reps in August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: We hired two. One started two weeks ago, the other's coming on the 19th. So we're almost there. The new guy, I've been sitting with him on calls, which is why I'm living in the QA tab lately.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Makes sense. Okay, tell me about the agents. What are you seeing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So this is the thing I emailed you about. When the voice agent transfers to one of my reps, the context doesn't come through.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The rep picks up and the caller starts over. Name, address, what they want, all of it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay. So the transfer itself happens, the call connects, but the rep doesn't get what the the agent collected.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Right. The note that's supposed to land with the call is empty. There's a note field, it's blank. So my rep is asking 'how can I help you' and the customer is like 'I already told the robot all this.'

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And it's not just annoying. On a solar call, if the customer already gave the address and and the utility and the roof type, and then they have to say it all again, we lose them.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: These are people who filled out a form forty seconds ago.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Last Tuesday I pulled, I don't know, eleven transfers, nine of them had the blank note. So it's most of them, not all of them.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So, okay, that's really helpful. When did you first notice it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Maybe three weeks ago? It was around when we changed the the routing on the Spanish queue, but I honestly don't know if that's related.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Got it. Can you send me a couple of call IDs where it happened? Even two or three. I'll take it to the I mean, team and come back to you with what they find.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, I'll grab them after this. I've got them saved in a sheet already.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Perfect. [PERSON_3], anything you you want to add on that?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll add this. My boss asked me last week, point blank, whether we're renewing. And this handoff thing, the agent losing the context, that's the first thing I thought of.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So I need to be able to tell him something.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: When do you need to have that conversation?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: He wants a read by the end of the month. I'm not saying we're walking, but I can't go in there with 'it's being looked at.' I need a real answer.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Understood. I mean, Let me get the call IDs, get it in front of the right people, and I'll come back to you with a status, not a maybe.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Give me until Thursday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thursday works.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Um, okay. Anything else on the tracking side, the Google Ads conversions, all that?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's been fine. No complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good. I'll send a calendar hold for Thursday, uh, say 11 your time, and [PERSON_2], just drop the call IDs in the thread whenever.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Will do. Thanks, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks both. And [PERSON_3], good luck with the soccer, so, [PERSON_2].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], hey [PERSON_2]. How's the Hartford weather treating you? I saw it was supposed to rain all weekend.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It did. My daughter's soccer game got rained out Saturday, so we ended up at the mall instead. Not the plan.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Same here. I spent most of Saturday on a Genesys upgrade that got pushed to next month anyway.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Oh no. Well, at least it's out of the way. Let's jump in. I wanted to walk through Q3 numbers and then spend most of the time on QM, since that's the thing we've been watching.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sounds good. Before that, just so you know, we're onboarding two new agency groups in November, so call volume is going to bump.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: How much of a bump are you expecting?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Probably twelve, fifteen percent. Medicare Advantage open enrollment starts the fifteenth, so it's going to be heavy through December.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. So looking at the um, numbers, you did about 41,000 calls in Q3, up from 38,500 in Q2. Signal AI is classifying around 93 percent of them, which is right in line with what we see at your size.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, that tracks. PreSense screen pops have been solid. The Genesys routing piece has been fine too, no complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. And Google Ads? Conversions still flowing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, that's been clean. Actually, the thing I wanted to raise is on the Salesforce side. Not the Google piece.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So we have a custom object for call outcomes, and our team keeps adding fields to it. Last month someone added a new field and a couple new picklist values, and the Invoca sync just stopped writing to that object.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Stopped entirely, or stopped for the new field?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Entirely. Nothing was landing. We caught it after about a week because an ops manager asked why her dashboard was empty.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I had to rebuild the field mapping in Salesforce to to get it flowing again, but any time we touch that object I'm worried it'll break.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. How often are you changing that object?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Maybe once a quarter. It's not constant, but it's enough that it's a problem. I can send you the timestamps and the field names.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Please do. I'll take that back to the team and see what we can find out. I don't want to guess at it on the call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I'd second that. [PERSON_2]'s been dealing with it, but it costs us visibility every time.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. Okay, QM. Where are you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Behind. We're at about 40 percent of calls scored, and we wanted to be at 80 by now. Part of it is just the rollout to the P&C side took longer than we thought.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Is it the seat provisioning, or is it the scorecards themselves?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Mostly the I mean, scorecards. The default criteria are fine as a starting point, but they don't match how we actually coach.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: For Medicare we have required disclosures, and for P&C the calls look completely different.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So you want to build your own criteria.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Right. And not just build them, weight them. A new agent who's three weeks in versus someone who's been here four years shouldn't get scored the same way on the same rubric.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We want to weight the criteria differently for new versus tenured agents.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And different scorecards by call type?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Ideally, yes. A Medicare enrollment call and a homeowners quote call shouldn't share a rubric at all.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. I'll write this up and bring it to product. I can't promise anything on timing, but I'll make sure they see the specifics.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's all I'm asking. If it helps, I can send over our current scorecard in a spreadsheet so they see what we're working with.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That That would actually help a lot. Okay, housekeeping. Renewal is next July, so we'll start that conversation in the spring.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Anything else on your list?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Nothing from me. Oh, one thing, are you the one handling the new seat adds, or do I go through support?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Send them to me and I'll route it. How many?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Probably six, for the two new groups. I'll get you names by Friday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. I'll send a recap this afternoon with the Salesforce timestamps request and the scorecard writeup. And [PERSON_1], good luck with open enrollment.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks. We'll need it. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hi [PERSON_1], hi [PERSON_2]. Can you hear me okay?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We can. Good to hear from you, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: How's everything on the lending floor this week? I saw a slight dip in total calls last Tuesday but it bounced back.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, that was our own doing. We had a team training on the new ARM products that morning, so the floor was thin until about 11.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Plus two of the loan officers were out. Reggie had a family thing and [PERSON_4] was at a closing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Makes sense. Volume looks healthy otherwise. You're pacing around 14,200 calls for September, which is up roughly 6% over August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That tracks. We added four loan officers last month too, so I'd expect that to keep climbing into Q4.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. And PreSense is still routing by intent without issues?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Fine. No complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Great. [PERSON_2], you had a couple of things you wanted to walk through?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I do. Both are things I've been collecting since the summer, and I finally have enough examples to describe them properly.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: First one is on the Signal AI side. Because we're regulated, anything a transcript or an AI summary exposes has to be controlled.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Right now the redaction we get is not configurable at the level our compliance team wants.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: What do you mean when you say the level?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: We need to pick which identifiers get masked, and we need it driven by role. A loan officer shouldn't see a full Social Security number on a transcript, but someone in compliance reviewing a complaint should be able to unmask it, and that unmask action needs to land in an audit log showing who viewed what and when.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So configurable redaction plus role-based access plus an audit trail of transcript views.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Exactly. Our examiner asked me in July how we'd prove who had seen a given transcript, and I did not have a good answer.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. That's clear. I'll write it up with your compliance angle and take it to the product team. Can you send me one redacted example and one that should have been redacted but wasn't?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I can. I'll pull two from September and send them this afternoon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. What's the second one?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The Salesforce integration. When we change a field on the Loan Application object, or add a picklist value, the call data stops writing to the custom object.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's the one that bit us in August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Right. We added a 'Property Type' picklist value for condos, and calls just stopped landing on the object. No error on our side, nothing in the call record, just silence.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: How did you catch it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Reggie noticed his call notes weren't showing up on his applications. Took us about a day and a half to figure out it was the mapping.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And once we refreshed the sandbox in September we had to rebuild the whole mapping from scratch, which is a lot of manual work for one person.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So the change itself and the sandbox refresh both break the mapping.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Does it recover on its own, or do you have to intervene every time?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: We intervene. Every time.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Send me the ticket numbers and the dates, and I'll attach them. Anything else broken, or is that it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Quality Management is working fine for us, for what it's worth. We're scoring about 4,000 calls a month now, which is more than we did in the spring.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: The loan officers grumble about it, but they grumble about everything.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. Anything you want me to look at there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, we're good.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Then let me get both of these written up. I'll have the Signal AI item in front of the product team by Wednesday, and I'll keep you posted on what they say.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That works. I'll send the examples and the ticket numbers today.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: One more thing before we go. Your renewal is next April. Do you want to put a business review on the calendar for January, so we're not doing it at the last minute?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: January is good. Maybe the second week?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll send a couple of options.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks both. Talk soon.

turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], how's it going?

turns.text: Good, good. Busy week. We're finally past the shoulder season rush, so I can actually breathe for a minute.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's the window I was hoping to catch you in. Thanks for making time. I know the renewal's on the calendar for January, so I figured we'd do a real working session now rather than scramble in December.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, that's smart. December is a mess for us anyway with the holiday scheduling across the branches.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Before we get into the renewal piece, how are things running? Call volumes holding up across the fourteen branches?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: They are. We're right around 21,000 calls a month now, maybe a little more. Charlotte and Raleigh are carrying most of it, Greensboro's been creeping up too.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's up from what I had, which was closer to 19,000 in the spring. Nice.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's the electrical side, mostly. We added two trucks in Raleigh in August and the call flow followed.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: How's the staffing on your end holding up with that? I know you had somebody out for a while.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We did. [PERSON_3] was out on leave through the summer, she's back now, which helps a lot. She's the one who actually lives in the platform day to day.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good, glad she's back. So the Google Ads piece, are the offline conversions still landing the way you expect? That's the thing I want to make sure isn't quietly broken before we talk numbers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: As far as I know it's fine. [PERSON_3] checks the match rates weekly and she hasn't flagged anything to me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Great. And PreSense, now that it's been in since the spring, any operational headaches?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, it's been quiet. The branches that have it like seeing where the caller came from before they pick up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, that's what I wanted to hear. So let's talk about the renewal itself. Where's your head at?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Honestly, the renewal is fine in principle. Nobody's looking to leave. The problem is procurement.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, say more.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Finance and procurement are pushing back hard on the way the add-ons are billed. They see Call Tracking on one line, then PreSense on another line, and then they start asking why the seats and the minutes are all separate.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So it's the structure more than the total?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's the structure. They keep saying they don't want to pay for three or four separate things that all show up under the same vendor.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: What they want is one bundled price for everything we use, one number, one line item, done.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. And is this coming from a specific person over there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's mostly [PERSON_4] in procurement. He owns the vendor review, and he's the one who flagged it. He's not wrong that it's confusing to read, but he's also not the one who has to make the platform work.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Sure. When does he need something in hand?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: He wants the renewal package to be one consolidated number. If it comes through with separate line items for the add-ons again, he's going to kick it back and we'll be doing this in January instead of now.

turns.text: That's helpful, and I'd rather know that today than in December. Let me take that back to our team and see what's possible on the packaging side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]

turns.text: No, the routing is fine. It's just staffing. We're managing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_3], while we're on the call, there's something I want to flag about the Google Ads side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Sure, go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So we send our call conversions to Google Ads, right? And they're showing up one to three days after the call. Sometimes longer.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Is that causing a problem for you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It is. Smart Bidding looks at those days and thinks we had no conversions, so it pulls back spend. Then the next day it sees them and pushes back up. It's like a yo-yo.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We've seen that. Last week Tuesday looked terrible in Google Ads, then Wednesday it caught up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Right. And our cost per lead bounces around because of it. The BDC gets fewer calls on those pullback days, then it's slammed when the spend comes back.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: How long have you been noticing the delay?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: A few weeks. I first saw it maybe mid-September. I thought it was a Google thing at first, but I checked the timestamps in Invoca and the conversion isn't sent until later.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Are you seeing the conversions in Google Ads eventually? Nothing missing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: They all show up. Just late. And since we're optimizing for calls, the delay messes with the bidding.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. I'll take this back to the team. Can you send me a couple of examples? Call IDs and the times they hit Google Ads?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, I can pull a few from yesterday and last week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. And is this happening on all seven stores or just some?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Looks like all of them. I checked Tulsa and Broken Arrow mostly, but the pattern is the same.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I can help pull the list too. I have the call logs.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That would help. Send whatever you have by Thursday and I'll get it to the right people.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Will do.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Anything else on the Google Ads side? Or Salesforce?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Salesforce is fine. Leads are writing over like they should.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, no issues there. The BDC sees the call record and the outcome.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. And Signal AI? Any changes you want to talk about?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No, it's working. We still get appointment booked and quote given tagged. That's all we use.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. I noticed your call volume went up about 15% month over month. Is that from the new GM's push?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, he wants more leads from search. He's been asking a lot of questions about how we track everything.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Makes sense. Anything he's asking that I can help with?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not right now. He's just getting up to speed.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: He did ask me about Marchex last week. He used them at his last group.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Well, if it's helpful, I can put together a quick summary of what you're using now and the results. Not a pitch, just the numbers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That might be good. He likes data.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll send something over next week. On the delay, I'll follow up once I hear back from the team.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sounds good. Oh, one more thing. We're doing a hiring event on the 20th, so the BDC will be short-staffed that afternoon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Noted. Do you want me to pause any alerts that day?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, we'll be fine. Just wanted you to know if you see a dip in answer rates.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. I'll keep that in mind. Anything else before we wrap?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's it for me. Thanks [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Same here. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks both. I'll send the follow-up by Thursday. Have a good one.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: evergreen pest & lawn / invoca Call notes, [PERSON_1] B. Tue 10/6 12:45pm

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: ashley still the only one running marketing for all six branches. said they hired a new office person in durham last week, so call handling might look different for a bit. didn't catch name. she's training.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Sept volume, rough from her side: about 2,100 inbound across the six locations, up maybe 8% from August. Fayetteville & Wilmington numbers climbing w/ the fall lawn stuff. Raleigh flat.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Her email pasted below, she sent it while we were talking so I'd have it:

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: "[PERSON_1], pulled the conversion report in google ads for sept 1 to sept 20 & put it next to our call log. the calls happened on the day, but the conversion dates in the column are two, sometimes three days later. same call, different date. so when i look at what smart bidding did that week it's working off a picture that's still filling in. i don't know if that's just how it works or somethng on our end. can you check?"

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: we pulled three examples live. call 9/4, conversion shows 9/6. call 9/11, shows 9/13. call 9/15, shows 9/18. she's right, it's a 2 to 3 day gap between the call date and the date sitting in that column. weekly reporting is what she lives on, so by the time she pulls monday numbers the weekend calls aren't in yet. asked me if she should stop looking at same-week numbers. told her not yet, let me take it to the team.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Her exact words at one point in the call (transcript): "It's not wrong, it's just late. & I make spend calls on Monday."

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: To do: - send her the export steps for the conversion date column so she has it documented - flag the lag to the integrations folks, medium, not an outage, reporting accuracy - ask her whether the lag is the same on both ad accounts or just the main one

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: she's out the week of the 19th for a family thing. Next call push to 10/27 or 10/28. She has a board thing first week of Nov so don't put it there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: she asked if we were at the pest conference in Charlotte, said she skipped it this year.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: signal ai she says is fine, no issues. didn't get into it, we were on the google thing most of the call.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: renewal's a long way out, may. she did mention she keeps getting mail from callrail. didn't ask for anything, just mentioned it.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: follow up thursday w/ the export steps.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Frontier notes 10/6

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] + [PERSON_2], 11:30

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: sept 41.2k calls, up 6% mom. peak mon/tue 9-11a. [PERSON_2] short two on the overnight five9 queue, training class of 4 starts 10/19.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: "we're exporting the presense and qm numbers to csv every monday and then someone hand-builds the [PERSON_2] deck. what i'd really want is a scheduled export into google sheets, so the branch vps open a link & it's just there."

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: "[PERSON_2] for me, I pull the Five9 side by hand. If I could point Looker or Sheets at it on a schedule, that's my Monday gone."

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: asked whether daily or weekly, which fields, who consumes it. taking it back to the team, no promise on timing.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: rest of the qm side: fine. signal ai catching appointment booked & quote given as expected. salesforce loan application objects writing clean, no dupes since the august mapping pass.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Pasted from this morning's spot check (call 10/6 08:14):

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: "...so the rate lock is 45 days, & i can email you the disclosure today."

turns.speaker: CALLER
turns.text: "Okay. & the appraisal, is that out of pocket?"

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: "it is, i'll put the number in writing."

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Email thread, [PERSON_2] to [PERSON_4], 10/3: "[PERSON_4], heads up, we have a compliance walkthrough the week of 11/9. Can you confirm the QM scorecard version we're on before then?"

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: To-do: - send [PERSON_1] the sheets export question in writing - check scorecard version for [PERSON_2], before 11/9 - cnfirm 10/19 training headcount, does overnight need coverage - Nov check-in? [PERSON_1] out 11/20-11/27

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: [PERSON_1]'s moving the Dallas office to a smaller floor in January, contact center staying put.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: renewal 4/30/27, nothing to do yet.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Keystone Mutual / Invoca | check-in | Tue, Oct 6, 2026

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], hey [PERSON_2]. How's the week going over there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_3]. Busy, but fine. Open enrollment stuff is behind us, so we're mostly just watching call volume settle back down.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, it's been steady. We're running around 11,000 calls a week across auto and home, give or take. The weekends are always the wild card.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good to hear. Any staffing shifts I should know about?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We finished moving the last of the overflow folks onto the Genesys queues last month, so we're fully on one platform now. Three hundred and some licensed agents. Nothing dramatic.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's a big milestone. Does that change anything about how the Invoca numbers are attached to agents?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not really. Same tagging, same reporting. Honestly the PreSense piece has been the bright spot lately.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Oh? Tell me more.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Agents really like seeing the pages a caller browsed before they pick up. It gives them something to work with right away, and it's helping them close more of those calls that started as digital shoppers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, the screen pop with the ad and the pages viewed, that's been a nice change. My claims folks use it constantly.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's great to hear. I'll note it for the account team.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: How about on your end, anything new with the platform I should be tracking?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Nothing major. I want to walk the QM scorecards with your team before the end of the quarter, just to make sure the weights still match how you're coaching.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's fine. We can pull in whoever needs to be there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Also, how's the after-hours AI Voice Agent pilot going?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's early. It's handling the overnight claims intake, mostly simple stuff, and transferring to a live person when it gets complicated. We're watching it closely through October.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Actually, [PERSON_3], can I bring something up? There's one thing that's been biting us.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Of course, go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Signal AI is flagging legitimate after-hours or weekend callers as spam. So real customers are getting pulled out of our reporting entirely.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hmm. How long has that been happening?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Few weeks. The weekend calls are the worst. Saturday and Sunday nights, we're losing a big chunk of the calls that should be counted.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Do you have examples you can share? Even a handful of call IDs would help.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, I'll pull a list together and send it over. It's not every call, but it's enough to skew the numbers we show leadership.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Let me take that back to the team. What's the impact on your side right now?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Mostly reporting. The claims numbers we report up the chain are off, and it makes the after-hours team look like they're not getting the volume they're actually getting.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's been a topic in our ops review for two weeks now. We just want it fixed so we can trust the numbers again.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. I'll flag it with the team today and follow up with you both by end of week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Appreciate that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Anything else on the reporting side I should know about?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, everything else looks fine. The Google Ads conversions are matching cleanly, and Salesforce is writing the call outcomes the way we expect.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. And Adobe Analytics?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's fine too.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Alright. Let's plan to check back in two weeks, same time. Does Tuesday at 3:15 still work?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Works for me. [PERSON_2]?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Fine by me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll send the invite and a short note on what we covered. Talk soon, both.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thanks. I'll get you those call IDs.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hi [PERSON_1], how's it going?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_2], pretty good. Busy week. We had two practices short-staffed, so so I'm covering front desk at the Meridian location this afternoon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: How about you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Oh, hanging in there. Lots of Q4 planning on my side. Thanks for making time. I know afternoons are hectic.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, no problem. Let me just close my office door so I can actually hear you.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. So I I pulled your account before we hopped on. Call volume looks steady. You're around 3,400 calls last month across the 19 practices, which is up a bit from August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, that tracks. September is always a little bumpy with school schedules. A lot of new-patient calls, which is what we care about.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Right. And I saw the Signal AI setup is classifying new patient versus existing patient pretty cleanly. Anything there feel off?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that part's fine. The practice managers read the call summaries every morning, that's just part of their routine now.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. And how's the Google Ads side looking? I know that's the piece tied to your new-patient budget.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Um, so that's actually the thing I wanted to bring up. The offline conversions do make it into Google Ads, they show up, but they're landing one to three days after the call. Sometimes longer if it's a weekend.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, so the conversions arrive, just not same day.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Right. And the problem is Smart Bidding is looking at that data while it's still incomplete. If I've got 40 new-patient calls on a Monday and only 12 conversions have posted by Tuesday morning, the algorithm thinks Monday was a bad day.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Uh, so it pulls back.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And then the rest of the week's budget gets set off that picture.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Exactly. I can't make daily budget calls. I've basically stopped adjusting bids intraday because I don't trust what I'm seeing. Uh, I just let it run and hope the weekly view evens out.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. How long has it been like this, do you think?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I noticed it uh, maybe... six weeks ago? End of August. I kept thinking it was a reporting delay on Google's side, but it's consistent.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. And is it all campaigns, or certain ones?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: As far as I can tell it's all of them. We run separate campaigns by service line, implants, general, ortho referrals.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: They all lag.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. I don't want to guess at what's happening there. Let me take this back I mean, to our team and see what's going on with the timing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Can you send me a couple of call examples, dates and the GCLID if you have it? I know that's a pain to pull.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Uh, yeah, I can grab a few from last week. I'll email them over tomorrow morning.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Perfect. And if it helps, note which campaign and the day the conversion showed up versus the call date. That'll give the team something concrete.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Will do. Honestly I mostly wanted to make sure I wasn't imagining it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No, that's a real thing to flag. Thanks for walking me through it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sure. Sorry, one sec, my front desk line is blowing up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Take your time.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay, sorry. Where were we?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The uh, conversion timing. I've got it. Anything else on the Meta side while we're here?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Meta's fine. We're not spending much there right now anyway.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. Let me look at a couple of other things. Your tracking numbers, are they all still mapped right? Any new locations since we last talked?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No new locations. We're still at 19. Though we're opening a satellite in Nampa in the spring, but that's a 2027 thing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Um, Good to know. We can plan for that closer to the time. And seats, you're at 22, still accurate?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah. We added a marketing coordinator in July, that's the 22nd. She's mostly doing content, but but she pokes around in the call data sometimes.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Um, okay. I'll keep that in mind for anything I send over.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sounds good. Oh, and before I forget, can we move our next check-in? I've got a board thing the first week of November.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, of course. What about the the second week?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Like, Second week works. Tuesday or Wednesday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll send an invite for Wednesday the 11th, same time.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Perfect.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So I'll chase the conversion timing with the team, and you'll send the examples. Anything else that's top of mind?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that's the big one. Everything else is running. I've got to get back out there, the waiting room is filling up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Go, go. Thanks [PERSON_1]. Um, Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks [PERSON_2]. Uh, Bye.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks for jumping on, both. I know this was short notice. [PERSON_1], [PERSON_2], how's the week going over there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Busy. We're two weeks out from the Q4 push and I've got three rooftops short a BDC rep, so I'm covering some of that myself.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Same here. Month end close is next week and I've got auditors in the building, so I'll keep my part tight.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. I put thirty minutes on the invite, and I don't think we'll need all of it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good, because I want to talk about money. December's renewal is on the calendar, and I have a competing bid in front of me that comes in noticeably lower per rooftop than what we're paying you.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Can you tell me who that is and what's in the scope?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Marchex. And the thing that keeps catching my CFO's eye is that their per-rooftop number already includes call scoring, so on paper it's roughly a thirty percent gap at our current rooftop count.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's a real gap. What's the rooftop count they quoted against, all twenty-two?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: All twenty-two, across both states. He had it on one page with no implementation fee attached, which is what made him forward it to me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: From my side it's less about the headline number and more that their bundle gives me scoring as a line item I'm already paying for separately today.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. I'm not going to argue pricing on this call, I don't own that. What I'd like is the quote itself so I can bring it into the renewal conversation with the right people internally.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I can forward you the PDF tonight. It's dated last Thursday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect, send it to my normal address. And remind me, is the scoring they're describing per call or per rooftop?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Per rooftop. That's the whole pitch, one number, everything's inside it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: While we're on it, nothing's broken on our end. Call tracking and the signals are doing what we expect. This is a commercial question.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good to hear. How's volume looking this month?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: We're tracking around eleven thousand calls for September across the group, up maybe four percent from August. Phoenix and the two Vegas stores are carrying most of that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And the tax season bump you usually see in February, is that still the plan?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, that's when we lean on it hardest. Our BDC schedules around it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, I'll make a note. Anything on the scheduling side I should know before we set the next review?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Only that Thursdays are bad now, we've got the regional ops call at nine. Tuesday or Wednesday afternoons work better for me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll move it. Let's say the twentieth, two o'clock your time?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That works.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Before we wrap, I want to be clear this isn't a threat. I'd rather keep the platform we have. I just can't walk into a renewal with a lower per-rooftop bid in my folder and nothing to say about it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's fair, and I'd do the same in your seat. Timing-wise, does your CFO want an answer before the December first date or is that flexible?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: He'd like something in writing by mid-November so it can go into the budget cycle.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Mid-November, okay. Let me take that internally, along with the quote, and come back to you with a real answer instead of a maybe.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's all I'm asking.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: One small thing, is the reporting you send us monthly going to keep coming through the same way? My team saves those.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Nothing changing there, they'll keep landing the same day each month.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
