turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:14 Okay so, renewal. Your term's up at the end of January. I figured we'd talk through where things stand and what you're thinking.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] DeLuca 1:25 Yeah, and, uh, that's kind of why I wanted to be on this one. I mean, I'm looking at a couple of options right now, and I've got Marchex in the mix.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:38 Okay. Can I ask what's driving that?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] DeLuca 1:41 Honestly? The line items. Finance went through this year against last year, line by line, and they they came back with questions I didn't have great answers for.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:54 Like what?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] DeLuca 1:56 Like, why are we paying separately for PreSense, and the QM seats, and then AI Voice Agent minutes on top of that. Three different lines for what, from where I sit, is one phone system. Procurement's the um, one actually pushing on it, not me.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 2:12 And I'll be honest, I didn't even know the Voice Agent minutes were billed that way until [PERSON_2] showed me the invoice.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:21 Okay. So the ask is really about how the add-ons are packaged and billed, not whether they're working.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] DeLuca 2:28 Right. I don't have a complaint about what it does. I have a complaint about how it shows up on a page.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:38 That's fair. I want to take that back and get you something concrete, not just a verbal. Can you send me the invoice breakdown Finance was looking at? That way I'm working from the same page they are.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] DeLuca 2:52 Yeah, I I can get that over to you this week.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:58 Perfect. Now, tell me how things are actually running. [PERSON_3], what are your call volumes looking like?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 3:05 We're averaging about 4,200 inbound a month across the group. Tulsa and Broken Arrow are the bulk of it. I mean, the BDC's handling most of the follow-up.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:17 And the Google Ads conversions still flowing through okay?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 3:23 Yeah, that's the part I'd fight to keep. We're pushing call conversions back into Google Ads and the Smart Bidding's been solid. Last month we had, uh, I I want to say 380 calls matched back to campaigns.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:37 Good. And Salesforce?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 3:39 That's fine too. Leads land so, on the BDC's queue like they should.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:45 Okay. Anything on staffing I should uh, know about, just so I'm not surprised later?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 3:51 We lost one BDC rep in September, so we're running lean. Should have somebody new in by early November. It's been a little chaotic on Mondays.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:03 Mondays are always the worst anyway.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 4:06 You're not wrong.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] DeLuca 4:08 Hey, quick thing. My daughter's got a a tournament in Kansas City the weekend of the 24th, so if we need to do anything in person, it's got to be before then.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:20 Noted. I don't think we'll need in-person, but good to know.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] DeLuca 4:25 Appreciate it.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:27 So here's what I'd suggest. Let me pull the billing breakdown, and I'll come back to you you with a couple of ways the add-ons could be structured at renewal. I'm not going to promise a number on uh, this call, because I'd just be guessing.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] DeLuca 4:46 That's all I'm asking. I just need something I can put in front of procurement that isn't, uh, 'trust us.'

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:53 Understood. Give me a week, maybe ten days.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] DeLuca 4:57 Works.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:58 And [PERSON_3], if you want to loop me in on anything with the new BDC hire, happy to do a refresher on the reporting side.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 5:09 Yeah, that'd be helpful. I'll ping you once we've you know, got a start date.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 5:16 Great. Uh, Anything else before we hop off?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] DeLuca 5:20 Nope. Thanks for making time.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 5:23 Thanks, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 5:25 Talk soon, guys. Um, Go enjoy that weather.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] DeLuca 5:29 Will do.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Ridgeway Motor Group working session Wed, Oct 14, 2026, 10:30AM • 6:05

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:07 Morning, [PERSON_2]. How's Tulsa treating you? Traffic on the way in was actually not terrible for once.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:14 Morning. Yeah, it's been one of those weeks already. We We had two people out in the BDC so I've been on the phones myself since Monday.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:23 Oh man. How's the queue holding up?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:27 We're getting through it. Probably a couple hundred calls a day across the rooftops, so it's not insane, but when you're down two bodies you you feel every one of them.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:41 Uh, yeah, I bet. Do you want to start with the Google Ads piece? I know that was the main thing you flagged.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:51 Yeah, let's do that. So, uh, our agency, the guys who run our paid search, they sent over a deck last week. They're saying we should take a look at CallRail.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:05 Okay. What's their angle?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:07 The pitch is that they sync conversions into Google Ads same day. Like, call comes in, it's in the account by end of day. And the quote they sent is lower than what we're paying, so the GM is asking questions.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:24 Got it. And this is coming from the agency directly, or is it something the GM brought up on his own?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:32 Bit of both. The agency recommended it, and then our new GM, he started in August, he's been going through every vendor line by line. So it landed at a bad time.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:45 That makes sense. What's the timing he's working against, is there a date on it?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:53 He wants a recommendation by early November. Not a renewal thing, our contract runs to the end of January, you know, but he wants the comparison done before budget planning.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:06 Okay. So what I'm hearing is the specific claim is same-day conversion sync, and the number on the quote is lower. Do you know what's in their quote, like how they're counting seats or calls?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:22 I don't have the detail on that yet. Honestly it was one slide and a price. I can send you you the deck if that helps.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:34 Yeah, send it over. I want to see what they're actually comparing, because a lot of the time those quotes are scoped to to one rooftop or one campaign, and you've um, got seven stores.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:47 Right. Um, and to uh, be fair, the thing that actually matters to me is whether the conversions are um, landing right. If Google's not seeing the good calls, our Smart Bidding drifts and then the lead quality drops and I'm the one hearing about it.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:07 Yeah. How are you feeling about what's landing now, just in terms of what you can see in the Ads account?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 3:14 It's fine. I mean, we're not sitting here chasing missing conversions. It's more the speed question they raised. I don't have a number for you on it.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:26 That's fair. Let me take the speed piece back to the team and get you something concrete, rather than me guessing at it on a call. And I'll ask them to look at how your setup is configured, because with seven rooftops and the number pools you've got, uh, there may be something in the routing that's worth checking.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 3:47 Okay. Just so I can tell the GM something, what's the turnaround on that?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:53 Give me until Monday and I'll have a written answer for you, something you can forward.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 4:01 That works.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:03 In the meantime, is there anything on the Salesforce side I should know about? I saw the BDC leads are still writing over.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 4:11 Yeah, that's all fine. No issues there.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:15 Good. And the signals, appointment booked, quote given, those are still matching what your team expects?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 4:22 Yep, no complaints. We've been using those in the Monday review and they're holding up.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:30 Great. Okay, what else did you want to cover? Um, I had down that we'd look at the campaign naming since you added the two new stores.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 4:42 Oh, right. Yeah, the two new rooftops, we've got tracking numbers on them but the campaign names are a mess. Half of them say the old store name from when we acquired the franchise.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:56 So the reporting's getting muddled?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 4:58 A little. When I pull the weekly numbers I have to remember which ones map to which store, and if I'm out, whoever covers for me won't know.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 5:08 Okay. That one I can actually help with. If you send me the list of what each one should be called, I can walk your team through the rename so the history stays intact.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 5:23 Oh, that'd be great. I'll get you the the list by Friday.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 5:29 Perfect. And how's the hiring going for the two open seats? Is that close?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 5:36 We've got one offer out. The other one, we're still interviewing. Hopefully by the first week of November we're back to full strength.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 5:46 Good. Anything else before I let you get back to the phones?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 5:51 No, that's it. I'll send the deck and the naming list. Thanks, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 5:57 Sounds good. Talk Monday. Hang in there.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 6:00 Ha, I'll try. Bye.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Coastal Comfort Mattress check-in Wed, Oct 14, 2026, 12:45PM • 4:46

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:02 Hey [PERSON_2], [PERSON_3]. How's Tampa treating you? Still hot down there?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:08 Oh, it's brutal. I walked from the parking garage to the building and I think I lost five pounds.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 0:16 And half the office is out this week, so so it's been quiet on our side.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:24 Ha, I bet. Well, I saw the volume ticked up a bit last month. Um, You're uh, at what, around 46,000 calls total across the 64 showrooms?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:35 Yeah, 46,300. We're up about 11% from August. Part of that is um, the AI Voice Agent taking a lot more store-hours and order-status calls. We went from 5% containment to almost 20% in six weeks.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:50 That's a big jump. Is that mostly after hours or during the day too?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 0:57 Both, but the after-hours transfer rate to Amazon Connect is way down. We used to have someone on till 9 PM for the Florida stores, and now we only have two people on the late shift.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:11 Good, good. And that's helping the queue, uh, I assume?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 1:16 Yeah, wait times during peak are down maybe 40 seconds on average. Nothing crazy but noticeable.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:23 Nice. Okay, so I know you wanted to talk about a couple things. What's on your list?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:31 Well, um, one thing that's been bugging me. Every Monday, [PERSON_3] or someone on her team pulls the previous week's dashboard data out of Invoca as a CSV, then manually pastes it into Looker for the exec report.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:45 Uh, okay.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:46 It's not a disaster, uh, but it takes 45 minutes. And the numbers are always a day behind because of when the export runs. I'd love it if we could just... have the dashboard metrics delivered automatically.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:02 Delivered how? Like a scheduled email, or something else?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:06 No, to Looker. Or Google Sheets, or honestly any BI tool. Something where we can hit an API endpoint and pull the numbers on a schedule. We have a data team that builds all our exec dashboards off the Looker instance, and this is the one thing they can't get programmatically.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 2:28 Like, yeah, I'm the one doing the export right now. It's fine for now, but as we add more campaigns, it's not going to scale.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:39 Got it it. So the ask is an API for dashboard metrics, so you can pull them into Looker or Sheets on a schedule and kill the manual export.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:52 So, Exactly. That would save us hours a month and let the data team own it instead of [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:00 Okay, that makes sense. I can take that back to product. I don't know what the roadmap looks like for that area, but but I'll log it properly. Can you send me a quick note after this with the specific dashboards you'd want? Just so I'm not guessing.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 3:19 Yes, I'll send it this afternoon.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:22 Perfect. Anything else?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 3:23 Not really. PreSense is working the way it should, Google Ads is fine, Meta is fine. We're actually seeing better match rates on the offline conversions since we switched the GCLID handling in September.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:38 Nice, that's good to hear.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 3:40 Oh, one other thing, totally unrelated. We're doing a big anniversary sale the first week of November. Should I let you know just in case we need extra support on the tagging side?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:53 Yeah, definitely. Send me the dates and I'll make sure nothing blocks you. Do you expect the same volume or higher?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 4:03 Probably 30 to 40 percent higher for that week. It's our biggest of the quarter.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:10 Okay, I'll flag it internally. And I'll also check that your Amazon Connect flows are ready for the burst. Last time we had a small hiccup with the queue overflow.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 4:22 Yeah, that was fixed, but good to double check.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:26 Alright. So I'll follow up on the API idea, and you'll send me the dashboard list and the sale dates. Anything else before we wrap?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 4:37 Nope, we're good. Thanks [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 4:39 Thanks [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:42 Thanks, both. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good morning, [PERSON_1]. Good morning, [PERSON_2]. How are things in Austin?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Morning, [PERSON_3]. Busy as usual. We're in the middle of Q4 push, so every lead counts.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hola, [PERSON_3]. The Spanish team is doing well. We added two reps last week, so we're up to twelve now.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's great to hear. How are the call volumes looking across the three states?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Steady. We're seeing about 2,400 calls a month from Google Ads and Meta combined. Texas is still the biggest chunk.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And a good portion of those are Spanish speakers. The AI Voice Agent handles the after-hours ones, which helps a lot.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. Any issues with the Salesforce sync or the Google Ads conversions lately?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, those are fine. The offline conversions are matching well. But I did want to mention something that came up last week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Sure, go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We got a pitch from CallRail. They're saying they can sync conversions to Google Ads the same day, and their quote came in noticeably lower than what we're paying now.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. How did that land with your team?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It got some attention. Our CFO asked why we're not looking at it. I told him we've got a lot invested in Invoca, but I wanted to flag it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: From my side, the Spanish team relies on the call recordings and the signals. If we switched, we'd lose that history.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I appreciate you telling me. Can you share the quote they sent? I can get our team to look at the comparison.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, I'll forward it after this call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks. Now, is there anything else on the account side? I saw your usage ticked up in September.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That was probably the Phoenix campaign. We ran a big push there for a week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Makes sense. And how's the new messaging agent working for follow-ups?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's fine. The team uses it for appointment reminders. No complaints.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. I also wanted to check if you need any refresher training on Signal AI Studio. I know you built a few custom signals earlier this year.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: We're okay for now. The ones we have are working. Maybe in Q1 we can look at more.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Sounds good. I'll note that. Anything else coming up? I know renewal is a ways off, but just want to keep a pulse.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Nothing urgent. We're focused on hitting our Q4 numbers. But that CallRail thing is the main thing on my mind.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. I'll take that back to my team and see what we can do. I'll follow up by early next week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Appreciate it, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thanks, [PERSON_3]. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks, both. Have a good rest of your week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], how's it going? How's the weather up in Tulsa today?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not bad, not bad. A little chilly this morning, but the the sun's out. How about you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Same here. I'm just trying to get through my coffee before the next call. So, I know we've got the renewal coming up in January.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Wanted to check in, see how things are going, and talk through any questions you might have.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, appreciate that. Things are mostly fine operationally. We're seeing decent call volume. Um, we're probably averaging around 11,000 calls a month across the seven rooftops.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: The BDC team is at full strength now after we hired two new people in September. So that's helped.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good to hear. And the Google Ads call conversions, still flowing through to Smart Bidding okay?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: You know, yeah, that's fine. No issues there. Our marketing guy, uh, [PERSON_3], he's been managing that. But look, I gotta be straight with you.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: The renewal is not a slam dunk this time.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, tell me more.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So, um, you know I came in August. New GM. I'm looking at all our vendor spend, and my boss, the regional VP, is asking me point blank whether we should renew with Invoca or take a hard look at Marchex.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And I'll be honest, the thing that keeps coming up is the billing structure.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The billing structure how?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Finance and procurement, they push back on paying separately for every little thing. You know, PreSense, QM seats, AI Voice Agent minutes.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And then Signal AI, we're paying for that as an add-on on top of call tracking. So when they see the renewal invoice, it's like, wait, we're already paying for call tracking, why is this other line item so big?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It creates friction.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. You know, so um, it's not necessarily the total number, it's the way it's broken out?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, I think that's fair. It's the add-on pricing friction at renewal. That's what I keep hearing. And honestly, when my boss asks me, 'Are we getting enough value to justify all these separate charges?', I don't have a great answer.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Like, I mean, we use Signal AI, but it's another line item. So yeah, it's a real question mark for us.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. That's helpful to hear. Let me, uh, I can take that back to our team. I don't want to promise anything on the the call, but I can see what options might be available.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Can you tell me a little more about how your boss is framing it? Is it purely cost, or is there something else?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Mostly cost. I mean, he's not saying the product is bad. He's just saying, you know, we need to tighten up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And when he sees all these separate charges, it makes him wonder if we're overpaying. So, so it's a real risk.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I'm not gonna lie, if we can't get comfortable with the pricing structure, we might not renew.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Understood. I'll bring that back. Let me ask, is there anything else that's coming up? Any other concerns?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, I mean, uh, everything else is fine. The BDC team uses it every day. No complaints there. Just the billing thing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. So let me, uh, I'll talk to my manager and see what we can do. I can't promise anything, but I'll come back to you with something concrete.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Um, How's that sound?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That sounds good. I appreciate it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Great. And, uh, I mean, just like, so I have it, are you still the main point of contact for the renewal, or should I loop in someone from finance?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: You can keep me as the main contact. I'll handle finance. You know, just, you know, keep me in the loop.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Will do. And hey, how's the new GM role treating you? Settling in okay?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's busy. A lot of moving parts. But it's good. I like the team here. We're just trying to get our processes tightened up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I hear that. Well, let me get on this pricing thing and I'll follow up with you by early next week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Does that work?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Um, yeah, that works. Thanks, [PERSON_2].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No problem. Uh, Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Take care.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Coastal Comfort Mattress / Invoca | working session | Thu, Oct 15, 2026

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Morning, both. Thanks for making time. How's the week going down there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Morning [PERSON_1]. Busy. We're a week into the fall mattress promo, so it's all hands.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah, same on my side. October's always heavy.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Do you have five minutes of housekeeping first, or should we go straight into the AI Voice Agent numbers?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Let's do the numbers first, then I've got one thing I want to walk through with you.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Perfect. So I pulled the last thirty days. You're at about 41,200 calls, up maybe six percent month over month.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That tracks with what we saw on the paid side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And the Voice Agent is handling around 9,800 of those, mostly the store-hours and order-status intents.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Which is roughly where we wanted it. It's offloading the easy stuff so my people can stay on the sales calls.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: How's staffing looking going into November?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: We're adding four agents on the eleventh. And I'm still short one supervisor on the weekend shift, but we're working on it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Which reminds me, [PERSON_3], I need to get you the updated headcount sheet.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Whenever. No rush.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay, what did you want to walk through?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So this is more of a heads-up than anything. Our agency, the paid media shop in Atlanta, they came to us last week and said we should take another look at CallRail.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: What's prompting that?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: They're pitching same-day conversion sync into Google Ads. Like, the call closes and the conversion lands in Ads the same day, and their quote came in under what we're paying you.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And to be fair, the agency is the one pushing it, not us. But they asked me to at least look.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Understood. Can I ask what the same-day piece would change for you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Honestly? Smart Bidding. We're running a pretty tight budget on the mattress category, and if the conversions land faster, the algorithm has more runway to learn inside the week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Right now we're looking at Monday numbers on Friday's spend, and by then we've already made the next day's decisions.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay, that's helpful. Let me take that back and get you something concrete rather than me guessing at it on the call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's all I'm asking. I told the agency we'd look, not that we were moving.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Do you know how they'd match the calls? Are they using the Google click ID the same way we do?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I didn't get that far into it. I can ask them.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll get you the agency's contact too, if that helps.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That would. I'll put together a side-by-side on the sync timing and send it to you both by end of next week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Works for me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Anything else on the platform side that's bugging you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: PreSense is fine. The screen pops are landing and the Amazon Connect side has been stable.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah, no complaints there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good. One scheduling thing, I'm out the last week of October, so if something comes up, ping the support line and they'll route it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Noted. We'll be fine, we've got the promo running.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Alright, I'll follow up with the sync comparison and the agency intro. Thanks, both.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thanks, talk soon.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Keystone Mutual / Invoca | working session | Thu, Oct 15, 2026

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], hey [PERSON_2]. How's the week going over there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Busy. We're down two supervisors on the auto side, so I'm bouncing between floors more than usual.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, and open enrollment for the home book is coming up, so claims volume is climbing. We ran about 41,000 calls through Genesys last month, which is up maybe 12 percent from August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That tracks with what I see on the Invoca side. Call tracking is showing the same lift, mostly from the paid search campaigns and a little from the direct mail landing pages.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good. Anything weird in the data before we get into the agenda?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Nothing flagged. PII redaction is doing its job, and the Genesys handoff is clean. What did you want to cover today?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Two things on my list, and one is just me saying thank you to the team. The AI call summaries have been a real help on the claims side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Tell me more about that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So when a first notice of loss comes in after hours, the agent used to spend five, six minutes reading the transcript before calling the customer back. Now the summary gives them the vehicle, the loss date, the police report number, all of it in one block, so callbacks are happening the same day instead of the next morning.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's good to hear. Is that on the auto side or across both books?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Mostly auto right now, but the home team started using it for water damage claims last week. My dispatch folks use it too when they're handing a tow over to the roadside vendor.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's helped with the handoffs between claims and the total loss unit. Less back and forth on what was already discussed with the caller.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay, I'll pass that along. What's the second thing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: This one's less fun. We added a new picklist value to the Claim Stage field in Salesforce, something our underwriting team asked for, and now the call records from Invoca aren't writing to our custom objects at all.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: When did you notice it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Late last week. Our Salesforce admin, [PERSON_4], caught it when a report came back empty. The standard task records still show up, but the custom claim object stopped getting the call outcome and the signal data.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And this started right after the picklist change?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Same day, as far as we can tell. We rolled it back for about an hour to test, and the records started writing again, so we're fairly sure that's the trigger.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. Can you send me the field name, the new value and a couple of example call IDs? I'll get it to the integrations team so they can look at how the mapping handles new picklist values.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll send that this afternoon. [PERSON_4] has the call IDs.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Perfect. I won't promise a date, but I'll come back to you with what they find.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Appreciate it. It's not breaking the contact center, but our claims leadership looks at those custom object reports every Monday, so the sooner the better.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. While I have you, how's the after-hours AI Voice Agent pilot going?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Quietly well. It's handling maybe 300 calls a week overnight, mostly FNOL and simple status questions, and it transfers to a live adjuster when someone asks for one. We're still keeping the sample small until the holidays.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Any changes you want to make before then?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not right now. We want a couple more weeks of data before we touch the flows.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Makes sense. Anything on the QM side you want to talk through?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No, that's been steady. We're scoring the claims queues every week and the supervisors are using it in their one-on-ones.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. One logistics thing, your renewal isn't until September of next year, so nothing urgent there. I'll still do a mid-year check-in in the spring.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sounds right. And I owe you a heads-up, we're hiring eight agents in November, so seat count will move a little.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks, I'll note it. Do you want me to set up a short call with the integrations team once they've looked at the Salesforce mapping?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yes, include [PERSON_4] and me. Mornings work better for us, Columbus time.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll aim for next week. Send me the field details and I'll take it from there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Will do. Thanks, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks both. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], how's it going? Sorry, I think I'm... there we go. Can you hear me okay?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_2]. Yeah, loud and clear. I'm in the truck today, so if it sounds weird it's just the road.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No worries. Are you driving? We can push this if that's easier.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No no, I'm parked. Just finished dropping flyers at the Durham office. It's It's fine.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay good. How's October treating you? I mean, I saw your call volume ticked up a bit versus September.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, we're up, um... I want to say 11 percent. Fall is always busy for us, people want the lawn treatments before winter and then the pest side picks up when everything comes inside.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Makes sense. Anything weird in the data on your end? I noticed the Raleigh number had a couple of quiet days last week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Uh, Oh, um, that was just Darnell out sick and then, you know, we had two techs at that training in Charlotte, so the routing was a little thin Tuesday and Wednesday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Back to normal now.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. Speaking of which, I wanted to check in on a couple of things before your campaign review next month.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: How's the Google Ads side looking?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's fine. Conversions are flowing. Nothing's broken, which is nice for once.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. So what's on your mind?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Two things. Um, the first one, honestly, is that I keep getting emails from a CallRail rep. Like, four in the last two weeks.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And the pitch is always the same, same-day conversion sync to Google Ads. They're saying we're losing bidding time, that if a call comes in at 2pm the conversion doesn't hit Ads until the next day so we're basically bidding on yesterday's information.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. And is that... are they quoting you anything specific?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: They came in about 20 percent under our current spend. Which, you know, I'm not going to pretend that doesn't get my attention.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Colby, our owner, he forwards me their emails now. He doesn't even say anything, just forwards them.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's fair. I'd rather hear it from you than find out later. Can you forward me the last one or two?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'm not going to promise anything on pricing in this call, but I want to make sure whoever needs to see it does, and I can at least get you a clear answer on what the sync timing actually is on our side.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, I'll send them over. It's not like we're unhappy, it's just... you know how it it is. Um, when um, the owner forwards you an email he's asking a question.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Totally. And you own Google Ads in-house, right? Nobody else touches it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Just me. Which is the other thing, actually.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So the spam flagging in Signal AI. It's marking real customers as spam. I was pulling the October numbers Monday and we're down, and I'm sitting there thinking, we are not down, the phones have not stopped ringing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So So I start reading transcripts. And there's this one, Saturday morning, 7:40. Caller says the street address, that's it. Eleven seconds.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Flagged as spam. That's a real person, [PERSON_2]. That's somebody standing in their yard looking at the wasp nest.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. So it's the short ones where they just give you the address.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's the pattern I'm seeing, yeah. Short calls, weekend, after hours, caller uh, gives an address and hangs up. The The system seems to think it's a robocall or a survey or something.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And it's not ten calls, it's more like 30 or 40 this month across the six locations, and those just vanish from reporting.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So my cost per lead looks worse than it is and I look like I don't know what I'm doing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: How are you catching them? Are you reading through transcripts one by one?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I filtered by spam and by call duration under 30 seconds, and then just, so, yeah, read them. It took me most of Monday afternoon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I only found it because a customer called back Tuesday and was annoyed nobody had followed up on her Saturday message.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. I want to get this in front of the right folks. Can you send me three or four call IDs?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The weekend ones especially, and the one where she called back, if you have it it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I can do like, that today. I already have a little list in a spreadsheet.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Perfect. I don't have an answer for you on this call, and I'm not going to guess at why it's happening.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll take the examples, get them to the team, and come back to you with what they say and a timeline.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's all I need. Um, I just don't want it to sit.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It won't. Anything else, or is that the list?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's the list. Everything else is quiet. Numbers are tracking right, the campaigns are set up the way we talked about in August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. One logistics thing, your campaign review is the first week of November, I'm thinking Tuesday the 3rd. Does 2pm work, or is that school pickup?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Ha, uh, 2pm is fine, pickup's at 3:15. Tuesday the 3rd, put it on the calendar.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Done. And I'll send you a note after this with the call ID format so you know exactly what to pull.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Great. Hey, I'm going to run, I've got a tech waiting on me about a truck. Thanks for listening on the spam thing, seriously.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Of course. Send those over when you get a chance. Talk soon, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Will do. Bye [PERSON_2].

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Cedar Ridge Dental Group / Invoca | check-in | Thu, Oct 15, 2026

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Morning [PERSON_1], morning [PERSON_2]. How's the Hillcrest office doing this week?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It's a little crazy. We have one hygienist out on leave until early next month, so I'm juggling the schedule and covering some of the front desk shifts myself.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, and it's showing up in the numbers. Total call volume across the practices is about 4,100 for September, which is actually up from 3,800 in August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's a solid increase. Is that mostly new patients calling the Boise locations, or are you seeing it everywhere?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Mostly Boise and Meridian. New-patient calls are what we're really bidding on in Google Ads, so that's where I'm watching most closely.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. How are the call summaries landing with the practice managers these days?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I check mine every morning when I get in, before I even open the schedule. It's a quick way to see which new callers actually booked and who I need to follow up with.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Same for most of the managers. It's part of the morning routine now.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good to hear. Anything else on your end that's been on your mind?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: One thing. I keep getting emails from a CallRail rep saying they can sync call conversions to Google Ads same-day, and their quote is lower than what we're paying for our setup.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: How often are they reaching out?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's been about once a week for the last month, and it's getting a little hard to ignore when the price is that different.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That makes sense. I can't speak to their timing, but I'll take that back to our team so we have a clear picture of what you're being told.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay, I just wanted you to know what's landing in my inbox.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I appreciate it. In the meantime, how are the Google Ads conversions looking on your side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: They're coming through fine. I checked yesterday and the numbers matched what I expected.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: And the Meta side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No issues there either. I just glance at it every couple of days to make sure nothing's broken.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Speaking of scheduling, [PERSON_3], can we get an export of last month's calls by location? I need it for our monthly ops meeting next Tuesday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Absolutely. I'll pull that together and send it over by Friday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Perfect, thank you.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Anything else before we wrap up?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that covers it. Thanks, [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Sounds good. Talk soon, both of you.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Coastal Comfort Mattress / Invoca | check-in | Thu, Oct 15, 2026

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hi [PERSON_1], [PERSON_2] here. How's the week going in Tampa?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_2]. Busy, but that's the usual. We're heading into mattress season, apparently.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Is that a real thing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It is if you're in retail. October through December, people decide they hate their old bed before the holidays.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Makes sense. I pulled some numbers before the call. Looks like you're tracking around 41,000 calls a month across the 64 showrooms now.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's right. September was 40,200, I think. We added two stores in August, so it'll keep creeping up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: How's the Amazon Connect side holding up with the extra volume?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Fine. My call center manager, Priyanka, says the routing is behaving. We did add three agents last month, so we're at 38 in the center now.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. And the AI Voice Agent for store hours and order status?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's doing what we asked. About 22 percent of calls get handled without a live agent now, mostly the 'are you open' and 'where's my delivery' stuff.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's a solid share for two use cases.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It is. And honestly, the team stopped complaining about it, which is the highest praise you'll get from a call center.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll take it. Anything you want me to look at while we're here?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: One thing, and it's not urgent. It's about reporting.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So every Monday, one of my analysts, Hector, pulls CSVs out of Invoca by hand. Call volumes by showroom, by campaign, the PreSense screen pop data, all of it. Then he pastes it into Looker and into a couple of Google Sheets that the regional managers live in.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Every Monday, same routine?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Every Monday. It takes him most of the morning, and if he's out, nobody else knows the sequence. Last week he was at a wedding and the Southeast region got their numbers on Wednesday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So the ask is scheduled delivery into Looker and Sheets, so nobody's hand-carrying files.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Right. Same reports, same cadence, just pushed on a schedule instead of exported by a person. If it could also hit a BI tool directly, that would help, because we're moving more of this into Looker anyway.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Is it just the weekly set, or are there other reports Hector's pulling?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Mostly the weekly. Sometimes he does a monthly rollup for me and for finance, but that one he can live with.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. Who else touches these once they land?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: The eight regional managers, plus me, plus finance at month end. So maybe fifteen people downstream of Hector's export.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. I'll write it up and take it to the product team. I don't want to promise anything on timing, but I'll make sure it's logged with the detail, the Looker piece and the Sheets piece.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's all I'm asking. Nobody's angry about it. It's just one of those things that quietly eats a morning a week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Totally fair. Anything else on the list?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Google Ads and Meta are both fine. We're not touching the campaign structure until January.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. Do you want me to pull together a quick review of the AI Voice Agent handling before your January planning? Something you can show the store ops folks?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:05 Do you have a couple of call IDs you can send me? I um, want to take this to the signal team and get it looked at properly. So, I'm not going to guess at what's happening.

turns.speaker: unknown

turns.speaker: unknown

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 3:42 Will do. I just want it fixed before the holiday push. Thanksgiving weekend is our biggest after-hours volume of the year, and if half of those calls get buried as spam, we're flying blind.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:54 Understood. I'll open it with the signal team today and ask them to look at the weekend angle specifically. I'll come back to you with [PERSON_4] [PERSON_4], but I can't promise a date yet.

turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:12 I will. Switching gears a little, how's the Genesys side holding up with the extra after-hours you know, volume?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 4:22 It's okay. We added six agents to the overnight queue last month, so the transfers are getting picked up faster. Average wait is under two minutes now.

turns.speaker: unknown

turns.text: [PERSON_3] 5:01 It's fine. We're still calibrating with the supervisors, but no issues.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: [PERSON_2] sends call IDs, I take the spam flagging to the signal team, and we'll regroup. Do you want to keep our regular check-in for two weeks from now, or wait until I have an update?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Morning, [PERSON_1]. How's the rain treating you up in Tacoma?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Oh, you know, it's October in the Northwest. My commute was basically a car wash. How about you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Sunny down here in Denver, sorry. Okay, so, before we get into it it, how did the member call volume look in September?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Let me pull it up... yeah, we ended around 18,400 tracked calls. That's up about six percent from August.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Nice. Is that mostly the auto loan campaign?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Um, Mostly, yeah. And the HELOC stuff picked up a little. Oh, and we had a staffing change, uh, Marcia left the contact center, so [PERSON_3]'s covering her queues for now.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. Do you need me to send anything over for the new folks, like a refresher on the QM side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Maybe later. Right now I want to talk about something that's been bugging me for a couple of weeks.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Sure.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So our Salesforce sync, the standard stuff, Leads, uh, Contacts, those all look fine. But the custom objects we built for loan inquiries and member outreach? They just stopped getting call data.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: When did you first notice?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: About two weeks ago. And here's the thing, it only broke after we added a field and changed a picklist on those objects.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Standard objects are totally fine.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So the writes just aren't landing on the custom objects.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Correct. Nothing in Salesforce. We can see the calls in Invoca, but nothing shows up on the custom side. It's a gap for my reporting and it's driving me a little nuts.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, that's helpful. Can you send me the object names and the fields you changed? I'll hand it to uh, the integrations team with your examples so they can dig in.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, I'll email you today. Honestly it's medium at worst, the standard objects cover most of what we need, but I do want it on the the radar.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Understood. I'll log it and come back to you with next steps. Separately, how's the QM scoring going?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good. Compliance signed off on the scorecard changes last month, so we're set there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Great. And the Signal AI signals, still behaving?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, um, those are fine. Oh, one small thing... can we move our next session to the 30th? I've got a board prep thing on the 23rd.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The 30th works. I'll send an updated invite.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Perfect. So you'll follow up on the Salesforce thing once you hear back?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yep, I'll keep you posted. And if [PERSON_3] needs anything on the QM side, just point her my way.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Will do. Thanks, [PERSON_2].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Anytime. Stay dry out there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], how's it going? How was the drive down from Tampa? Wait, no, you're already in Tampa. Sorry, I just got off another call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Ha, no problem. Yeah, I'm in Tampa. It's still stupid hot for October, but we survived. How about you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Can't complain. Busy week. I saw the AI Voice Agent had a big jump in handled calls last month, that's good to see.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, we're at about 11,400 calls a month now across the 64 showrooms, and the agent's taking maybe a third of them for store hours and order status.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: You know, our night shift in the call center is down to four people, so it's helping. But, um, that's actually not why I wanted to talk.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay, shoot.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So something's off with the Google Ads side. Our offline call conversions, the ones you all send over, they're not landing until one to three days after the call. And I mean consistently.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We had a call Monday at 10am, conversion didn't show up in Google Ads until Wednesday night.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. So when you say landing, you mean you can see the conversion in Google Ads, it's just delayed?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Right. The call shows in Invoca same day, transcript and all. But Google only sees it a day or three later.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Which means Smart Bidding is out there making decisions on half the picture.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Got it. And when did you first notice this?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Mid-September is when I started staring at it. Our cost per lead on the paid search campaigns has gone from like $41 to $58 since then.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Same creative, same budget. It's not the market, I don't think.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Like, that's a real jump. Let me write this down. One to three day lag on offline conversions into Google Ads, started mid-September, CPL up from $41 to $58.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And to be fair, some of the campaigns are worse than others. The showroom ones are the worst. Um, but I don't want to overcomplicate it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: No, that's helpful. Do you know if the GCLID is coming through on those calls, like, or is it just the timing?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: The GCLID's there. I checked with our paid media person... sorry, her name's Renata, she runs the Google side... she pulled a few examples and the click IDs match.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's purely timing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. I want to take this back to the team and have them look at the send schedule on your account specifically.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'm not going to guess at a cause on the call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's fine. Um, I just need someone looking at it, because every day this drags, we're basically teaching the bidding algorithm wrong.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Understood. I'll open it today and you know, get you an update by, let's say Tuesday. Does Tuesday work?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Tuesday's fine. I've got a showroom walkthrough Monday anyway, in Savannah, so I'll be useless.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Oh nice, Savannah. Is that the new one?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Not new, we're remodeling it. New mattresses, new signage, the whole thing. Fun stuff.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: You know, Anything else you want me to look at while I'm in there? PreSense, the agent, messaging?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, those are fine. The screen pop thing... the agents like seeing what page the customer was on. And the SMS follow-up is doing its job.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Good. And the Amazon Connect routing, no complaints there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that's been solid. Okay, one more thing on the conversions, and then I'll let you go.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Sure.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: If it turns out the delay is on your end, can we get the backlog re-sent? Because those conversions from the last month are just sitting there, and Google's never going to learn from them if they trickle in this slow.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll ask about backfilling when I bring it to the team. I don't want to promise it it before I know what's happening.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Fair enough. That's all I've got.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Okay. I'll send a note today so you have it in writing, and update Tuesday. Enjoy the heat.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Ha, thanks. Talk soon, [PERSON_2].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], hey [PERSON_2]. Thanks for carving out time this afternoon. How's the week going over there?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Busy. We had two BDC folks out with the flu Monday and Tuesday, so I was on the phones myself half the week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Volume's actually up, we crossed about 2,300 calls last month across the seven stores.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Which is good and bad. Good for the pipeline, bad for [PERSON_1]'s voicemail inbox.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Ha, yeah. But the tracking side is fine, calls are landing on the right campaigns and the Google Ads conversions are flowing the way they should.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's good to hear. Anything on the Salesforce side you want me to look at while we're on?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that's working. Records are writing over fine, the BDC reps don't complain about it, which is basically a compliment.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll take it. So I wanted to spend most of this on the renewal, since we're a couple months out. What's the temperature on your side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll jump in. I came over in August, so this is my first pass at the contract. When I sat down with our controller, she went through this year's invoice against last year's line by line and the thing that jumped out was all the separate line items on top of the base platform.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Which ones stood out to her?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: PreSense is billed on its own, the quality management seats are billed on their own, the AI Voice Agent is metered by the minute.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: She asked me why we're paying four times for one phone call, and honestly I didn't have a clean answer for her.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's fair. I can't restructure line items from this call, but I want to get the details right. Can you send me the invoice she was working from?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I can. And I'll be straight with you, while she was doing that comparison she was also taking a call from Marchex.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: They came in under what we're paying now on a per-rooftop basis, and they were throwing call scoring into the number.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Per rooftop meaning per store per month?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Per store, flat, all seven of ours. And I've now had two conversations with a dealer group down in Oklahoma City that already made the switch.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So it's not just a cold pitch anymore, it's people I know.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. What are they telling you about it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Mostly that the math was simpler. I don't have a strong feeling about the product itself, that's not what's driving it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It's the paperwork.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. And [PERSON_1], is this the same conversation you're getting?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: From my side it's procurement. Every time something new gets added, it's a separate approval with a separate justification, and by the time we get to renewal it feels like we're re-buying the platform three more times.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: If that doesn't get easier, I can't promise we're not looking at what else is out there before January. I'm not saying we're leaving, but I'd be doing my job wrong if I didn't look.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: No, I'd rather know now than in December. Let me write down what I'm hearing: the add-on structure is creating friction with finance, Marchex is coming in lower per rooftop with scoring bundled, and that combination puts the renewal decision in question.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Am I missing anything?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's the shape of it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: One more thing, and this is smaller. The controller asked whether anything we're already paying for overlaps. I told her I'd ask.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll bring that to our team too, along with the invoice. I'm not going to improvise an answer on pricing on this call, that wouldn't help you.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Appreciated. I'd rather you come back with something real.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Who else needs to be in that conversation? Sounds like the controller.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Her name's Renata. She's the one with the spreadsheet. And if we get to the point of signing something, procurement gets a look.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. Send me the invoice and I'll set up a follow-up for later this month, and I'll get Renata on it so she's hearing it directly instead of through both of you.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That works. Her Thursdays are usually open after two.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll send a couple of options. Anything else on your end before we wrap?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: We're onboarding two BDC reps the first week of November, so if there's anything they need on the reporting side, I'll ping you separately.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Please do. And tell the two sick ones I hope they're feeling better.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: They're back and they're fine, they just have a lot of catching up to do.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Alright, I'll get the follow-up on the calendar. Thanks [PERSON_2], thanks [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thanks [PERSON_3].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Talk soon.

turns.text: Morning, [PERSON_1]. Thanks for making the time. How's everything on the dispatch floor this week?

turns.text: Morning, [PERSON_2]. Busy. We're into heating season now, so the phones are going pretty much nonstop.

turns.text: Honestly, the thing I keep hearing from the front line is how much they like the AI call summaries. It saves them a ton of time on callbacks and dispatch handoffs.

turns.text: That's good to hear. Can you give me a sense of how they're using them day to day?

turns.text: Sure. Say a customer calls about a furnace that's short cycling. Instead of the dispatcher listening to the whole recording, they read the summary, see what the tech needs to know, and get the job assigned. It used to take ten minutes, now it's two.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And the new hires, they ramp faster because they can read the summary before they even pick up the callback. Our last training class was up to speed in about half the usual time.

turns.text: That's a nice outcome. I'll pass that along to the team, they like hearing it. Anything on the PreSense side you want to talk about?

turns.text: How are things looking on your side with the Google Ads connection right now?

turns.text: From what I can see the conversions show up, it's just not instant. Usually I see yesterday's calls reflected by the next morning.

turns.text: Okay. So on the same-day piece, I don't want to guess at how we'd handle that. Let me take it back to the team and get you a straight answer on what's possible.

turns.text: That's all I'm asking. I'm not looking to switch over a few dollars, but if they're genuinely faster and cheaper, I'd be silly not to at least ask.

turns.text: Understood. I'll follow up by Thursday with something concrete.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: While you're at it, can you also send over a quick rundown of who on our side can pull reports? [PERSON_4] retired in September and her login is still floating around.

turns.text: Sure, I'll put together the user list with roles and send it with the follow-up.

turns.text: Appreciate it. One other thing, and this is small. Can we push our QBR to the first week of February? January is our slowest month and I'd rather not tie up [PERSON_3]'s morning.

turns.text: That works on my end. I'll send a calendar hold for the first Tuesday in February.

turns.text: Perfect. Oh, and tell whoever handles your invoices that the Raleigh address changed, we moved suites in the same building. The last one went to the old suite.

turns.text: I'll get that to billing today.
